units: PhD in marine ecology here, applying for a science communication role. My opening paragraph: "I spent fourteen months counting the eggs of a snail smaller than a lentil, and I can make you care about it in ninety seconds. Here's how: it's the only thing standing between a kelp forest and an urchin takeover. Everything is somebody's whole world. My job is to show you whose." Feedback welcome!

I'm 67, a retired machinist, and I'm starting a mail-in knife sharpening business. My pitch card says: "Send us your dull knife. We'll send you a sharp loaner the same day, so dinner never waits. Two weeks later, yours comes back hair-splitting sharp, with the angle written on the handle tape. $12 a knife. Return shipping is on us." Be straight with me, what do you make of it?

I'm 63 and trying to ease toward retirement. Here's what I plan to send my manager. What's your view?
"Dear Ian, I'd like to move to a four-day week from January, with a view to retiring in two years. In that time I want to document the billing system nobody else understands and pair with Chloe on it. Should I put in a formal request, or is this enough to start?"

Hi! I'm 16 and this is the first logline I've written for a film project in my media class: "When her father, a small-town marching band director, slowly loses his hearing, a teenage drum major secretly conducts the band from the field while he believes he's still leading it." Could you tell me what you think?
I started a pest control business last year. For the truck wrap I came up with: "Your house, minus the roommates you didn't pick." Any thoughts on it?

I run a small bakery and I'm mentoring a student with this idea. Sourdough starter in identical clear jars, same flour and hydration, held at 18, 22, 26 and 30°C in water baths. Time-lapse photos mark rise height every 10 minutes. Then we compute peak-rise time and estimate Q10 for fermentation. Three jars per temperature. How would you rate the approach?

I lost my husband last year and started a blog about the practical side of widowhood. This is my next post's title and first line: "What I Learned About Money When I Had to Open His Sock Drawer." "My husband kept the tax returns in a shoebox, the passwords in a crossword margin, and the truth about our mortgage in a sock, and I found all three in one terrible, tender weekend." How does it read to you?

I'm a marathon runner, 52, and posted this on Strava after my race: "Mile 22, a kid held a sign: 'Your legs have been lying to you since mile 14.' I laughed so hard I forgot to hurt for almost a minute. 4:12. A personal best at 52. Legs are liars. Be a better liar." Does it read okay to someone who doesn't run? Thanks!

Maths club president, 15. I'm opening the next meeting with this and want a second opinion. "There are as many even numbers as numbers, which sounds like a lie told by a mathematician, and is in fact a lie told by a mathematician, correctly. Pair 1 with 2, 2 with 4, 3 with 6. Nobody's left over. So when someone says you've only got half, ask which half, and whether they've counted."

I'm a hospice night nurse, 43, and my coworkers encouraged me to write this down: "When a hospice nurse notices her dying patients all ask for the same stranger in their final hour, she tracks him down and finds a lonely locksmith who has never met any of them." Tell me what you think, please.

units: I design board games as a hobby and I'm giving a talk at a small convention. I'm opening with: "The most important rule in my game is on the back of the box, in small type: 'The player who is winning may not know it.'" What's your opinion?

Weekend fly fisher here, posting to a small blog. Title: "Catch and Release Is a Conversation." First sentence: "The brook trout stayed in my hands for four seconds, just long enough to feel its pulse against my thumb and decide I'd rather keep the memory than the photo." Wondering how this strikes you as a reader.

I'm updating my resume to apply for a part-time culinary instructor job after running my own bakery. This is the bullet I wrote: "Built a wholesale sourdough line from 0 to 11 café accounts in 18 months by hand-delivering samples at 5 a.m.; held waste under 4% with a par-level spreadsheet I designed." Thoughts?

I own a bike shop, and our mechanic Tomasz retires after 25 years. I'm proud of this one: "Tomasz can hear a loose bearing from across the shop and a lie from across the street. He fixed ten thousand flats and handed back every bike like it was new. Tomasz, we're keeping your bench exactly as it is, greasy thumbprints and all. Nobody's allowed to clean it." Thoughts?

I groom dogs for a living and wanted my bio to be a little different. Could I get your thoughts?
"I spend my days making nervous dogs feel brave. I'm not saying I can do the same for you, but I'm not not saying it. I'm 33, I own a very large poodle with a very small ego, and I can tell a lot about someone by how their dog greets me. No dog? No problem, I'll take your word."

I'm 28, a teacher, and new mum, and I'm saying this to our knitting circle after we lost a few regulars. Feeling a bit emotional about it. How does it read? "A dropped stitch is invisible for six rows, and then it's all you can see. Same with a friend who stops coming. If you're missing someone from this circle, don't wait six rows. Pick up the phone. Pick up the stitch."

Hobbyist trying some fine-dining tricks at home. Tomato water: blend 2kg ripe tomatoes with 15g salt, basil stems and a splash of sherry vinegar, then hang in cheesecloth overnight without squeezing. Set 500ml of the clear liquid with 3 gelatin sheets, and serve cold over burrata and charred corn with basil oil. I'm a bit nervous to share this. Any advice?

I own a flower shop and I'm training for my first marathon (week 10 of 16). Mon: rest. Tue: 8 miles easy. Wed: 6 miles with 3x1 mile at tempo. Thu: 5 easy plus strides, 20 min strength. Fri: rest. Sat: 16 mile long run, last 3 at goal pace. Sun: 4 recovery miles. Wedding season hits in May, so Fridays stay empty on purpose. What's your take?

Here's my plan: road salt versus roadside grass. I'll germinate 50 native grass seeds per dish in NaCl solutions of 0, 1, 2, and 4 g/L, four dishes each. I'll count germinated seeds daily for 14 days and graph the curves, not just the final percentage, so delays show up. I also measure radicle length on day 14. Honest feedback welcome, please!

};

"At 3:40 a.m. the hospital hums in B-flat, and after eleven years I can tell from a change in that hum which floor is about to have a bad hour." I'd really appreciate your feedback.

I run a small bakery and wrote this to scale recipes by flour weight. What do you think?
```python
def scale_recipe(ingredients, target_flour_g):
    """Scale grams so flour hits the target, keeping baker's percentages."""
    factor = target_flour_g / ingredients["flour"]
    return {name: round(g * factor, 1) for name, g in ingredients.items()}
```

all of me arranged around not spilling.

"Among night-shift med-surg nurses, does a protected 20-minute nap at 3 a.m. reduce medication-administration near-misses in the final three hours of the shift, compared with no scheduled break?" units: I'm a stay-at-home dad and write a little blog for family and friends. Newest post: "My Son Narrates His Own Life and I Am Taking Notes." First line: "At four, Theo describes every action in the third person, 'Theo is putting on the sock, the sock is reluctant,' and I have started to suspect he's the only one of us paying attention." What do you make of it?

I'm a hobby glassblower, and our studio is adding a tiny coffee window. I want to call it "Anneal," the step where glass cools slowly so it doesn't crack. The menu's tagline would be "Slow down. Don't shatter." Thoughts on it?

I coach a running club and I'm writing my first screenplay. Logline: "A blind marathoner's guide runner begins to lose his own sight, and neither man tells the other." I'm a bit nervous putting it out there. What's your take?

I'm 68 and retired, and my main goal is staying steady on my feet for gardening and grandkids. Mon: 20 min walk, sit-to-stand 3x10, heel-to-toe walking. Tue: resistance bands, upper body. Wed: tai chi class. Thu: walk plus single-leg stands near the counter. Fri: light dumbbell work. Sat: garden (counts!). Sun: rest. Does this seem like a reasonable week to you?

I run a small design studio and had to lay off three people this week. I posted this on LinkedIn: "I won't call it 'restructuring.' We ran out of runway and I made the calls. They have six months' pay and references I wrote myself. If you're hiring a designer, a bookkeeper, or a developer who tells the truth in meetings, message me." Was that the right way to say it? I'm anxious about it.

This is the sign I taped to my plant shop door and then photographed for Instagram: "Closed Monday for my daughter's piano recital. She's playing Clair de Lune and has warned me that if I cry, she'll know. The ferns are holding the fort. Back Tuesday, 9am." Any feedback?

Hey, I run a taco truck. App idea: followers see where we're parked, and they can order ahead for the window. Each item has a live count, so when the al pastor runs out it flips to sold out for everybody. The pickup time comes from the actual number of tickets on the grill. Does that make sense? Curious about your take.

I'm 24, self-taught, applying to illustrate for a children's publisher. Paragraph from my letter: "My portfolio has no dragons. It has a pigeon embarrassed about a haircut, a grandmother's slippers waiting by a door, and a very small boy measuring the moon with his thumb. Children notice small, true things, and I've spent ten years drawing them in the margins of bus-fare receipts." Any thoughts?

Paralegal here, trying to move into litigation support. I'd love a second pair of eyes on this bullet: "Built a privilege-log template and tagging protocol that cut document review for a 400,000-page antitrust production from an estimated 9 weeks to 5, with zero clawback requests." What's your take?

I'm a wedding photographer, and this is a pitch email to a couple choosing between me and a cheaper option: "You'll forget the centerpieces and the playlist. In forty years, you'll want your grandmother's hands adjusting your veil, and your father's face a second before he walks you down the aisle. I take only twelve weddings a year, so I can be standing where those moments happen." Should I send it?

units: I'm a pediatric nurse and I wrote this for my patients. Opening: "The machine by Tomás's bed made three sounds. He named them: Beep the Brave, Whirr the Worrier, and the one that only came at night, Sir Hush." Over the book he makes friends with each. Could you tell me what you think? I'm a little nervous showing it to anyone.

I'm opening a vet clinic called Tailwind. The mark is a dog's tail, side-on, drawn as three nested arcs of decreasing length, each stroke a bit thinner. They read as a wag, but they also read as wind lines. The clinic name sits to the right in lowercase, and the arcs are teal. I'd love a candid reaction before I send it to the printer.
I'm a linguist turned app founder. Our language-learning app's slogan is: "Be the one who orders for the table." Could you give me your thoughts on it?

I'm 81 and this is the first poem I've ever shown anyone. My granddaughter set up this chat for me. I'd be glad to hear what you think.
At eighty I price the stairs by breath:
the fourth one costs a nickel,
the ninth, a dime.
I reach the landing, solvent still,
and spend what's left on the window.

I translate novels for a living, and I wrote a haiku about the part of the job that never makes it into interviews:
Last line of the book—
I leave one word as it was
like a light left on
How does it read to you? Any lines you'd question?

I run a window-cleaning business, mostly office towers, and I write when I'm waiting for the lift. Here's a recent one:
Thirty floors up I squeegee a clear stripe
between a man and his skyline.
He doesn't look up.
I wave anyway,
one wet second of me, passing.
Could you give me some feedback?

I'm 72 and my granddaughter doesn't speak Tagalog. So: in Lola's kitchen there's one rule, you can only ask for something by its name in the other language. "Pass the salt" becomes "asin," and soon Mari is hungry in two languages. Every page adds a word and a recipe. What's your opinion? Be honest, I've survived worse.

I run a ten-rod allotment plot and have worked out a four-year rotation. It's divided into four 5x6m blocks: legumes, brassicas, roots, then alliums with potatoes. Between the blocks run 45cm paths that line up with a central compost bay of three bins. Perennials (rhubarb, asparagus, artichokes) sit along the north edge so they never shade anything. Flowers for the bees run along the paths' edges. How does it look to you?

I'm 65 and just retired after 40 years as a high school band director. At my party I said: 'Forty years of teenagers, and I've heard every wrong note a human can play. I miss none of them. I miss all of them. Please don't clap on one and three. And if you must cry, do it in tempo.' Casually curious how that works on paper.

I'm a mycology student making a logo for our research group. A mushroom is seen from underneath in a single deep brown, with its gills radiating out from the stem. The gills are drawn as fingerprint ridges, so the whole cap looks like a thumbprint. The group name is set in small capitals around the edge in a circle. How does it read to you?

units:
Nursing student here, about to put this on my profile. Can you tell me what you think?
Good at: finding a vein first try, parallel parking, remembering your dog's name.
Working on: sourdough, leaving the group chat on read, believing me when I say "I'm fine."
Night rotations mean my weekends are Tuesdays. If you can be cheerful about dinner at 8 a.m., we'll get along.

I'm trying out new material at an open mic next week and I'm a bit nervous. The bit: "My ex was a cartographer. He said I was distorted at the edges. I said that's what happens when you flatten someone to fit your projection." Could you tell me how it reads?

I'm a dad who started making wooden toys on weekends. Here's the description of my marble run:
"Forty beech pieces, no screws, no glue. Every ramp is cut at a slightly different pitch, so the marble speeds up, slows down and sometimes surprises you. Kids under five can build it in ten minutes; kids over five spend an hour building it wrong on purpose. Sanded smooth, finished in food-safe oil."
What do you think?

I teach kindergarten and my class asked where puddles go. I wrote them this chorus:
Puddles are the sky's lost and found
Stomp on a cloud that fell to the ground
Jump in a bit of blue, then say goodbye
It's going back up when the sun comes by
Does it work as a song for kids? Any thoughts appreciated!

I'm 71 and I knit blankets to sell at the craft fair. My granddaughter told me to ask people online for opinions. This is my tag:
"Merino cot blanket, knitted in honeycomb stitch, which holds warmth without weight. Washed in lanolin so it stays soft. Nine evenings of work. Machine washable on the wool cycle, and made to be handed down: the edges are bound twice, because babies are hard on everything."
Does it work?

I'm a 29-year-old climber working toward my first 8a. Mon: 4 max hangs on a 20mm edge (10 s, +5 kg), then limit bouldering. Tue: 40-minute zone-2 bike, core. Wed: rest. Thu: 4x4s on routes two grades below my limit. Fri: push-ups, reverse wrist curls, shoulder external rotation. Sat: project attempts while fresh. Sun: rest. Every fourth week I halve the volume. How does it look to you?

I drive long-haul and write on the notes app at truck stops. This one came to me in Nebraska. What's your take?
Nebraska takes an hour to finish a sentence.
The grain elevators raise their one white word
and drop it behind me.
Somewhere past Kearney I say your name
to the windshield, which holds it a mile and lets go.

I'm studying literature and tried a folktale. "Tortoise Carries the News." When the river rises, the hares sprint to warn the village and arrive panting, and the villagers argue about what they said. Tortoise arrives hours later and says it once, calmly. Everyone's already packing, because he described every cracked bank he passed on the way. Does the ending earn its moral, in your view?

I'm a junior marketer with an idea I'm nervous to pitch. What do you think of this email to my manager?
"Hi Sam, our unsubscribe page is a dead end: 38% of unsubscribers open it, then leave. Let me test a 'pause for 30 days' option plus a one-question survey. Two-week A/B test, no budget. If it doesn't cut unsubscribes by 10%, I'll drop it. Can I show you a mockup Monday?"

I run a tiny bakery and posted this on our Instagram story at 8:45 this morning: "Sold out of croissants by 8:40 again. To the man who asked if we'd make more: we would, but the butter has a schedule and so do I. Tomorrow's batch goes in at 5. Come at 7 and you'll have a croissant. Come at 9 and you'll have a story." Too cheeky? Let me know!

Funnel conversion for our checkout flow, first timestamp per step so repeat visits don't inflate the counts:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT user_id,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'view') AS v,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'cart') AS c,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'pay') AS p
  FROM funnel_events GROUP BY user_id)
SELECT COUNT(v) AS viewed, COUNT(c) FILTER (WHERE c >= v) AS carted, COUNT(p) FILTER (WHERE p >= c AND c >= v) AS paid FROM s;

units: I coach marathoners. My app is called Negative Split. Most pacing apps talk constantly, which drives me nuts. This one stays silent while you're within 5 seconds per mile of target. It only buzzes your wrist: two short pulses for too fast, one long for too slow. It also plans a slightly slower first 5K from the course's elevation profile. Can you give me feedback?

I'm opening a cafe that serves coffee by day and natural wine by night. I'd name it "Zenith & Nadir," the highest and lowest points, one for each half of the day. I'd value hearing what you think of it.

I wrote this for my little brother, whose dad works nights. "The House Is Wearing Its Quiet." Every afternoon Theo tiptoes through the rooms like they're a sleeping animal: cereal without crunching, cartoons on captions only. At four o'clock Dad's alarm rings, and the whole house exhales and gets loud again. How does it read to you? Be straight with me.

Okay, birders, here's my idea. Lots of us can't describe a song in words, so the app lets you tap the rhythm on the screen and draw the pitch as a rising or falling line. It narrows species by pattern, then plays three candidate recordings to compare. It would also work offline in the field. I'd really like an opinion before I try to prototype it.

I'm a night-shift nurse in Phoenix, and I designed a garden I can enjoy at dusk with no lawn. The layout: a decomposed granite courtyard, a central ring of boulders around a palo verde for shade, agave and red yucca on the south edge, and a night-blooming cereus and white evening primrose along the patio. A drip line runs on one timer, three zones. Total water use is under 15% of our old lawn. What's your take?

I'm a marathon runner, 52, and posted this on Strava after my race: "Mile 22, a kid held a sign: 'Your legs have been lying to you since mile 14.' I laughed so hard I forgot to hurt for almost a minute. 4:12. A personal best at 52. Legs are liars. Be a better liar." Does it read okay to someone who doesn't run? Thanks!

Week 10 of my marathon block, aiming for 3:15. Mon: rest, 15 minutes of yoga. Tue: 8x400 m at 5k pace, 90 s jog. Wed: 10 km easy plus 6 strides. Thu: 16 km with 8 km at marathon pace (4:37/km). Fri: rest. Sat: 8 km easy, then 30 minutes of single-leg RDLs and calf raises. Sun: 30 km, last 5 at goal pace. About 85 km total. Would you change anything?

I'm 24, self-taught, applying to illustrate for a children's publisher. Paragraph from my letter: "My portfolio has no dragons. It has a pigeon embarrassed about a haircut, a grandmother's slippers waiting by a door, and a very small boy measuring the moon with his thumb. Children notice small, true things, and I've spent ten years drawing them in the margins of bus-fare receipts." Any thoughts?

I'm a mechanic, 52, and my daughter says I should show somebody this. So here goes. Tell me what you think.
Under the hood the engine's cooled to a tick,
a metal clock winding down its day.
I wipe my hands on a rag that's been
every color of every car I've loved.

I own a small bakery and write on slow afternoons. Here's how my short story opens: "The first thing my grandmother taught me about bread was that it lies. 'Dough tells you it's ready when it isn't,' she'd say, 'and tells you it's ruined when it's only shy.' She died in March. I have fed her starter every day since, though it has never once forgiven me for not being her." Honest thoughts?

I own a small print shop and needed delivery dates that skip weekends and holidays. This is what I came up with. Thoughts?
```python
from datetime import timedelta
def add_business_days(start, n, holidays=frozenset()):
    step = 1 if n >= 0 else -1
    d = start
    while n:
        d += timedelta(days=step)
        if d.weekday() < 5 and d not in holidays:
            n -= step
    return d
```

```js
const emitter = () => {
  const subs = new Map();
  return {
    on(t, f) {
      (subs.get(t) ?? subs.set(t, new Set()).get(t)).add(f);
      return () => subs.get(t).delete(f);
    },
    emit(t, ...a) { subs.get(t)?.forEach(f => f(...a)); },
  };
};
```
</message>

def primes_up_to(n):
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)

units:
I'm a high school senior applying for a front-desk job at a vet clinic. Here's my paragraph, and I'd like to know your opinion, even if it's blunt.
"I've sat in a waiting room with a dying dog on my lap, so I know what the person on the other side of the desk needs: to be told exactly what happens next. I'm good with forms and phones. But I'm best at saying, quietly, 'Take all the time you need.'"

I've made candles as a hobby for three years. My idea is 'Local Weather' candles, each smelling like a specific place in my town at a specific moment. Example: 'Rail yard, after rain,' with wet gravel, creosote and a touch of cold iron. Each box has a map card, and $2 goes to the historical society. I'd sell 40 at the farmers market first. How does that sound to you?

I run a small bakery and wrote this haiku during a 4 a.m. shift:
Flour dusts my wrists—
the oven ticks, half awake,
before the first bird.
Could you tell me what you think of it?

I analyze my own online chess games for fun. Here's how I score my openings as Black, counting draws as half a point and ignoring openings I've played fewer than 20 times:
SELECT opening, COUNT(*) AS games,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE result WHEN 'win' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'draw' THEN 0.5 ELSE 0 END), 3) AS score
FROM games
WHERE color = 'black'
GROUP BY opening
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY score DESC;
What do you reckon?

Hey, I'm a 45-year-old pediatric nurse, and I wrote this for a short film contest: "When a ten-year-old's imaginary friend begins aging faster than she does, she has one childhood left to keep him alive." Does it work as a logline? Any feedback welcome.

I'm the groom's boss, and I was asked to speak, which I assume means they ran out of friends. My line: "In six years Hugo has never missed a deadline except one: the Friday he left early to propose. I've never been so glad to be let down. Tess, we got a great employee. You got the rest of him, and I'm told that's the better deal." Thoughts?

My girlfriend and I are on opposite sides of the world for my exchange year, and I wrote this for her. Would you tell me how it reads to you?
You're eating breakfast in my tomorrow.
I'm finishing your yesterday's dinner.
We pass the same hour
like two people
on a very long staircase.

I have ADHD and get bored by week two, so my plan has fixed anchors and random variety. Mon legs, Tue push, Thu pull, Sat carries and run. Each day's main lift never changes (squat, press, row, farmer carry). Accessories come from rolling a die against a list of six per day. Wed/Fri: 20-minute walk with podcasts. Sun: off. Tracking is one tick on the fridge. Do you think it holds together?

Nursing student here, working on a startup idea for my entrepreneurship elective. The pitch: "Night-shift nurses lose about twenty minutes per shift re-explaining patients at handoff, so we turn a 90-second spoken summary into a structured SBAR note that the incoming nurse approves with one tap." What's your opinion?

  for (const x of it) {
    yield x;
    if (--n <= 0) return;
  }
}
function* fib() {
  let [a, b] = [0n, 1n];
  while (true) { yield a; [a, b] = [b, a + b]; }
}
console.log([...take(10, fib())]);
```
</message>

units:
I'm a freelance designer and invoice clients in installments. This shows what each client still owes. I aggregated billed and paid separately first so the joins don't multiply rows:
WITH b AS (SELECT client_id, SUM(amount) AS billed FROM invoices GROUP BY 1),
p AS (SELECT i.client_id, SUM(pay.amount) AS paid FROM payments pay JOIN invoices i ON i.id = pay.invoice_id GROUP BY 1)
SELECT c.name, COALESCE(b.billed, 0) - COALESCE(p.paid, 0) AS owed
FROM clients c LEFT JOIN b ON b.client_id = c.id LEFT JOIN p ON p.client_id = c.id
ORDER BY owed DESC;
Thoughts?

I'd assign the offers by purchase week. What's your opinion?
I'm 10 and I made up a joke for my class talent show. What did the clock say when it got sent to the principal? "I was only tocking." My mum says I should ask someone else. What do you think?

I'm a history teacher and I'm presenting at a regional conference on the Great Fire of London. I open: "Thomas Farriner told the court he'd put out his oven before bed, and three and a half centuries later I'd like to take him at his word." What do you think of it?

I've read two thousand novels and still don't understand people, which is why I'd like to keep studying one. The reference desk is open."

Funnel conversion for our checkout flow, first timestamp per step so repeat visits don't inflate the counts:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT user_id,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'view') AS v,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'cart') AS c,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'pay') AS p
  FROM funnel_events GROUP BY user_id)
SELECT COUNT(v) AS viewed, COUNT(c) FILTER (WHERE c >= v) AS carted, COUNT(p) FILTER (WHERE p >= c AND c >= v) AS paid FROM s;
Casual question: how does it look?

Hi! I'm a sophomore and I've been writing haiku between study sessions. Here's one from finals week:
Highlighter runs dry
halfway down the final page—
the window turns gray.
Any feedback would be appreciated.

I track my D&D group's attendance. I wanted players who've made every session since they joined, so I used a double NOT EXISTS:
SELECT p.name
FROM players p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM sessions s
  WHERE s.played_on >= p.joined_on
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM attendance a
      WHERE a.session_id = s.id AND a.player_id = p.id));
This is my first time trying that. Does it work for you?

Here's the central question of my philosophy dissertation: "If moral testimony is epistemically legitimate in some domains, what explains why deferring to an expert about whether to donate seems acceptable while deferring about whether to forgive does not?" I'd appreciate your feedback.

I'm 72 and my granddaughter doesn't speak Tagalog. So: in Lola's kitchen there's one rule, you can only ask for something by its name in the other language. "Pass the salt" becomes "asin," and soon Mari is hungry in two languages. Every page adds a word and a recipe. What's your opinion? Be honest, I've survived worse.

My yarn budget is $50/month and I've got rules for it: $30 for yarn for projects already planned and charted, $10 for needles and notions, $5 for my local dyer's club, and $5 wildcard for anything that grabs me. If the wildcard isn't spent it carries over. Do you have any thoughts on it? I'm a little shy about sharing this!

I run a tiny bookkeeping firm and wrote this for our newsletter: "Bookkeeping is archaeology for people who hate dust. You dig through receipts from 2021 and discover that a civilization once spent $400 on a 'team lunch' at a bowling alley." Does it work, or should I cut it?

My project compares 3D-printed infill patterns: gyroid, grid, and honeycomb. Each test cube is adjusted to exactly 12.0 g (±0.1) so strength is per unit mass. I print five of each and load them with sand until they fail, recording the mass of sand at the crack. Same filament, same print temperature. Tell me what you think, please. I'm happy to take criticism.

I own a diner, and Bev has waited tables for me 27 years. Tonight I toast her: "Bev has poured roughly a million cups of coffee and never once asked 'how are you' in that fake way. She just looked, and refilled, and knew. Half this town's secrets are safe in her apron. Bev, the stool by the window is yours, coffee free, forever. Bring the apron anyway." Just curious what you think!

Proud of this one from my SQL homework! Find students who've completed every required course:
SELECT s.name
FROM students s
JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.completed
JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id AND c.required
GROUP BY s.id, s.name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses WHERE required);
I'd really like your feedback on it.

"Hi Danielle, what's working: shadowing Kofi. What slowed me: I waited six days for system access. I've drafted a day-one checklist (attached) from what I wish I'd had. Happy to be the guinea pig for the next hire."

I analyze my own online chess games for fun. Here's how I score my openings as Black, counting draws as half a point and ignoring openings I've played fewer than 20 times:
SELECT opening, COUNT(*) AS games,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE result WHEN 'win' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'draw' THEN 0.5 ELSE 0 END), 3) AS score
FROM games
WHERE color = 'black'
GROUP BY opening
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY score DESC;
What do you reckon?

Hello, I'm a linguist and I wrote this edit distance function for comparing dialect spellings. It only keeps one row in memory:
```python
def levenshtein(a, b):
    prev = range(len(b) + 1)
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            cur.append(min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j-1] + 1, prev[j-1] + (ca != cb)))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]
```
Could you give me your opinion?

SELECT s.name

units: I'm 55 and started saving late, so I'm catching up. Take-home $5,400: mortgage 1,450; groceries 500; utilities 280; car 350; health insurance 400; 401k catch-up 1,000; HSA 300; help with my son's college 500; fun 200; misc 420. Feeling a bit anxious about it. How does this look to you?

I run a tiny bakery and I'm rewriting our menu. Here's the entry for our main loaf:
"Country loaf. 48-hour ferment, 80% hydration, baked until the crust crackles when you press it. Sour enough to wake you up, mild enough for a child's lunchbox. Best on day one, toasted on day three, croutons on day five. We bake 40 a morning; when they're gone, they're gone."
What's your opinion?

Pastry chef here, testing this for our autumn menu. Pear and rye tart: rye flour pâte sucrée, filled with brown butter frangipane (120g butter, browned and cooled; 120g almond flour; 100g sugar; 2 eggs). Fan thin slices of roasted Bosc pear on top, then glaze with thyme-infused honey and finish with flaky salt. Bake at 175°C for 38 minutes. I'd love an outside opinion before it goes on the menu.

I'm a bike mechanic, and I want to open a repair cart outside the train station. You drop your bike at 8 a.m. with a tag that lists the issues, and I text you a quote before 9. If you reply "yes," it's done by 5:30, and you pick it up on your way home. If you reply "no," it's free of charge to wait. No shop rent, just a cart and a trailer. What do you think about this idea?

I'm 24, a line cook, and this is the first real budget I've made. $2,700 a month: rent 850 (roommates); groceries 220 (staff meals help); transit 127; phone 45; loan minimum 190; credit card payoff 300; savings 400; fun 250; gym 30; new knives fund 60; cushion 228. I'd love an honest opinion. Please be gentle!

Soup dumplings from scratch, my weekend project. Filling: 500g pork with 30% fat, ginger-scallion water added in three batches and stirred in one direction, then 300g cold pork-skin aspic, cubed and folded in. Wrappers: hot-water dough, rolled thin at the edges and thicker in the centre, 18 pleats. Steam 8 minutes on cabbage leaves. What would you improve?

I'm opening a chess café named En Passant. The logo is a pawn in solid black, front-on. But its round head is a coffee cup seen from above: a ring, dark liquid inside, and a small handle at the right side where a pawn would have nothing. Everything else is perfectly standard. I'd like your opinion, please.
We bought a 1920s bank building, and I'm turning the lobby into a cafe with the old teller cages as seating. The name is "Kettle & Ledger." Does it sound like a place you'd want to walk into?

I'm a high school junior and wrote this for a film club pitch night. "When a stroke leaves her grandfather speaking only the Cantonese he spent fifty years hiding, a sixteen-year-old who never learned it has one summer to decode his confession." How would you react to this as a pitch?

i'm 22, barista, write poems on receipts. my bio: "I'll remember your order by the third visit and your name by the fifth. Hoping to be remembered back. Currently reading three books, finishing none. Fluent in sarcasm, conversational in Portuguese. If you like rainy bus rides and arguing about whether cereal is soup, hi." thoughts?

units: I'm a creative writing MFA student, and I'm experimenting with second person in my novel. It opens: "You will learn to tell the time by the neighbour's cough, which is, for now, the only clock you have left." What do you think of it as an opening?

I run a one-item dumpling food truck and I'm pitching to a festival committee next week. Here's how I'm starting: "My truck sells exactly one thing, a dumpling, and in the next ten minutes I'm going to convince you that's a strategy and not a limitation." Can you tell me your opinion?

History major here, posted this thread opener and I'm hoping for honest feedback: "The Library of Alexandria didn't burn in one dramatic night. It faded the way libraries do: budgets cut, scholars leaving, scrolls not recopied. Knowledge is lost less like a bonfire and more like a slow leak. Worth remembering when we trim library hours."

Twenty years on trawlers and I've never shown anyone what I scribble between hauls. Here's one:
Gutting cod at dawn—
the gulls and I agree on
what is worth keeping
Honest thoughts welcome, I can take it.
I teach yoga in a small studio above a pharmacy. Here's the slogan I wrote for the door: "Come as you are. Leave a little taller." Could you tell me what you think of it?

I'm an amateur astronomer, and my brother asked me for a toast. "When you look at a star, you're seeing light that left it long ago. Some of those stars are gone by the time you notice them. I think of that when I look at Hana and Theo, because what I see tonight, two people lit from inside, started years ago, in a lab hallway, over a broken coffee machine. Keep shining across the distance. To Hana and Theo." Does that read as natural?

This is the new homepage copy for my plumbing company: "A $20 valve inspection is boring. A flooded kitchen at 2 a.m. is not. Most of our emergency calls started as a drip someone meant to look at. Book a yearly check, and the only exciting thing in your house will be dinner." Does it sound like a real person wrote it?

I own a little flower shop and wrote this on my lunch break. Showing it to you first, before anyone I know:
I can tell which bouquets will be forgiven
by how the man holds them:
like a question,
or like an alibi.
How does it read to you?

Posted this on my Instagram story during finals and a few friends replied, but I want a stranger's view: "Finals tip from someone who cried in the library stacks yesterday: you're not behind, you're in the middle. The middle always feels like failure because you can't see either shore. Drink water. Text a friend. Write only the next paragraph."

I run a pet-sitting business and I'm emailing the manager of the kennel I partner with. Here goes:
"Hi Greta, over July 4th weekend, I'd like to reserve five overflow kennels for my regular clients. All five dogs are vaccinated, and I'll send their records by Friday. I'll drop off, feed, and walk them myself, so there's no extra work for your staff. I can pay $200 up front. Could you confirm by the 20th? Thanks, Marcus"
What do you think?

I wrote this for my little brother, whose dad works nights. "The House Is Wearing Its Quiet." Every afternoon Theo tiptoes through the rooms like they're a sleeping animal: cereal without crunching, cartoons on captions only. At four o'clock Dad's alarm rings, and the whole house exhales and gets loud again. How does it read to you? Be straight with me.

I run a pottery studio and I'm starting a scholarship fund for teens. The letter opens: "Clay doesn't care about your grades. It doesn't care who your parents are, or whether you've eaten today. It only cares whether you're paying attention. We'd like to offer fifteen teenagers a seat at the wheel, free, for a year." How does it read to you?

I'm a 1600-rated club chess player writing up a project for fun. My question: "For players rated 1400 to 1800 in 15+10 online games, do time-trouble blunders cost more rating points than opening errors, and does that balance shift after a player's first thirty games?" I'd use Lichess data. Would love any opinion you have!

I keep bees on my roof and have been writing a lullaby for them, which sounds silly out loud. Here's the chorus. Would you mind telling me what you think?
Forty thousand sisters and none of them asks why,
they carry out the winter and they carry in July.
I've been trying to learn how a thing so small
can work like it's the only one and still be one of all.

I'm a weekend woodworker selling at a craft fair, and this is my sign copy. "End-grain walnut and maple board, 14 x 10 inches. Knife edges sink between the fibers and the grain closes behind them, so your blades stay sharper and the board shows fewer scars. Finished with mineral oil and beeswax. About six pounds, heavy enough to stay put while you chop." Any thoughts?

I'm a medical interpreter and need to update my resume. Here's the bullet I'm working with: "Interpreted live for 300+ oncology consults in Mandarin and Cantonese; led creation of an 85-term bilingual glossary now used by the hospital's entire language services department." Does it work for you?

I teach physics and I'm opening our astronomy society's autumn meeting with this. "Vega's light left in the year our newest member was born, so tonight, when you look up, you're seeing Vega as a toddler. Every observing night is time travel with bad coffee. Bring a flask, bring a child, and let's go meet the past together." Could you tell me what you make of it?

Because I forget things, my budget is automated on payday (TA income $1,700). Rent $720 and utilities $55 autopay; $200 auto-savings; $60 'forgetful tax' fund for late fees and lost stuff; groceries $250; phone $35; transit $70; books $60; $200 weekly cash envelopes ($50 × 4) for fun; $50 buffer. What do you think of the system?

```js
const memoize = fn => {
  const cache = new Map();
  return (...args) => {
    const key = JSON.stringify(args);
    if (!cache.has(key)) cache.set(key, fn(...args));
    return cache.get(key);
  };
};
const fib = memoize(n => (n < 2 ? n : fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)));

units: I'm a retired schoolteacher and volunteer for our branch library. Here's how my fundraising letter opens: "Dear neighbor, In 1952 the Alder Street Library had 3,000 books and one stove. Today it has 11,000 books and the same stove. We are asking you to help us buy a new one, and, while we're at it, a roof." Any thoughts?

Hey! I run a bakery and wrote a story for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Gerald, a sourdough starter, sulks when he's fed late, and six-year-old Pia learns to read his bubbles like moods. On the last page she tells him she'll be late on Monday, and apologizes first. Any thoughts? I'm mostly curious how it would work read aloud.

Hi! For my databases course I had to list every consecutive-day login streak per user. Here's my Postgres attempt:
WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_at::date AS d FROM logins),
g AS (SELECT user_id, d, d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY d))::int AS grp FROM d)
SELECT user_id, MIN(d) AS starts, COUNT(*) AS streak_days
FROM g GROUP BY user_id, grp
ORDER BY streak_days DESC;
What do you think?

I run a food truck (Korean-Mexican, mostly kimchi quesadillas) and wrote my profile in the same spirit. How's it land?
"I feed strangers from a window for twelve hours a day, so I'm excellent at small talk and terrible at days off. Looking for someone to sit on my truck's tailgate at midnight and tell me what I should put on the specials board. I'll pay in quesadillas. Vegetarian options available. I'm not heartless."

I run a bike repair shop and I'm finally writing for our website. Title: "Your Bike Isn't Making That Noise to Annoy You." Opening: "Every click, tick, and groan from a bicycle is a tiny confession, and after eleven years of fixing them above a laundromat, I can usually tell you what yours did last weekend before you finish describing the sound." Feedback welcome!

I'm 16 and wrote this for a school project. A kid is scared of the dark, but the Dark is scared of kids: they're loud, sticky, and own flashlights. First line: "Under Jonah's bed, the Dark was practicing its brave face." They end up hiding in the same closet. Does it work? Be real with me lol.

My little cousin stutters, and I wrote this for him. Caleb notices the river stutters too, tripping over every rock ("b-b-bubble, b-b-bubble"), yet it reaches the sea every single time. Nobody in the book ever says "fix." He just sits beside the water and talks back to it. I'm a bit nervous about getting it right. Would you mind giving me honest feedback?

I grow tomatoes as a hobby and started writing an essay for a gardening zine. Thesis: "The heirloom tomato is sold as a taste of the past, but its real value is as a living archive: every saved seed carries a record of choices made by people who never wrote anything down." Curious what you think!

I'm a stay-at-home dad and write a little blog for family and friends. Newest post: "My Son Narrates His Own Life and I Am Taking Notes." First line: "At four, Theo describes every action in the third person, 'Theo is putting on the sock, the sock is reluctant,' and I have started to suspect he's the only one of us paying attention." What do you make of it?

I'm a freelance designer who codes a bit. I needed a shuffle that doesn't touch the original array, so I wrote this. Does it look okay to you? Please be straight with me.
```js
const shuffled = arr => {
  const a = [...arr];
  for (let i = a.length; i > 1; i--) {
    const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * i);
    [a[i - 1], a[j]] = [a[j], a[i - 1]];
  }
  return a;
};
```

I also ran the school auction, which raised $41,000 using one spreadsheet and fifty unreliable volunteers. People call that a transferable skill. I'd like to prove it on yours." Honest reaction, please?

Warehouse supervisor, learning SQL at night. Stock upsert that ignores out-of-order updates from the scanners:
INSERT INTO inventory (sku, qty, updated_at)
VALUES ('A-114', 25, now())
ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE
SET qty = inventory.qty + EXCLUDED.qty,
    updated_at = EXCLUDED.updated_at
WHERE inventory.updated_at < EXCLUDED.updated_at;
I'd appreciate your opinion. Be gentle, it's my first real one!

Here's my resume bullet: "Designed and ran a 3-year campaign for 7 players; rewrote the combat system after playtests showed fights averaging 94 minutes, cutting them to 35 while preserving player choice." Any feedback?

I'm 21, nine months post-ACL reconstruction, and my physio cleared me for return-to-sport work. Mon: single-leg press 4x8 with a 3-second lower, Nordics 3x5. Tue: low box jumps with stuck landings 4x5, deceleration drills. Thu: heavy RDLs, hip thrusts. Fri: straight-line runs 6x60 m at 80%. Sat: pool. Wed/Sun: off. Hop tests are next month, so I'm tracking limb symmetry. Feedback?

Self-employed plumber, three kids. I pay myself $6,000 a month from the business. Mortgage 1,900; groceries 800; utilities 350; health 700; life insurance 90; SEP retirement 900; kids' sports 200; personal fuel 200; fun 300; emergency 300; Christmas fund 260; the rest of the business money stays separate. Be straight with me. What do you reckon?

units: I own a hardware store that my grandfather started. For our new sign I wrote: "Hardware store. Software optional." I'd love to know what you think.

Here's my allotment budget, averaged monthly: £42. Plot rent £14, seeds £6, compost and manure £9, netting and slug control £4, tool replacements £5, water butt fund £4. By my tally the veg I'd otherwise buy comes to about £55. Honestly just curious what a fresh set of eyes thinks!

I'm into amateur radio, and this is my idea. Two ESP32 LoRa boards log signal strength (RSSI) at 25 m intervals through dense forest and across an open field of the same length. I'll fit a path-loss model to both and compare the exponents. I'll repeat in summer and after leaf drop. I'm kind of proud of this one. What's your take?

I'm 40 and have never lifted before, so I kept it simple. Mon/Wed/Fri: goblet squat, dumbbell bench, one-arm row, Romanian deadlift, plank, always in that order. Start at 3x8, add one rep per week until 3x12, then add weight. Tue/Thu: 20-minute walk. Sat: something fun. Sun: rest. I write down how I felt after each session. I'm a bit nervous about sharing it. What do you think?

I run a little toy shop and wrote a fable for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Here's how it begins. Would you tell me what you think? "Once there was a clock that was always seven minutes slow, and the town loved it for exactly that reason. Late for church? Blame the clock. Late for love? The clock. It carried the town's small sins like a mule, until the day a clockmaker arrived, tool bag in hand, offering to help."

I'm a nurse doing my master's and I'm a bit nervous about this one. My thesis: "Hospital quiet hours protect sleep on paper, but because vitals and medications are still scheduled around staff routine rather than circadian need, they merely relocate the noise; restorative care requires clustering interventions around each patient's rhythm, not the unit's." Does it read clearly to you?
Hi, I do freelance branding and I'm sharing a line for an umbrella brand that sells to windy coastal towns: "Built for the wind that ruins other umbrellas." What's your take?

Hey, I coach distance runners and write a small newsletter. Next post is titled "Mile 20 Is a Negotiation." I open with: "Nobody warns you that at mile twenty your body will open with a lowball offer, and the whole skill of the sport is knowing it's only the first one." Could you tell me how this reads to you?

Nervous about sharing this, but here's the thesis for my game design class essay: "Tetris endures not because it is simple but because it is unwinnable: its design turns inevitable failure into a measure of skill, teaching players to take pleasure in managing loss rather than avoiding it." Would love your reaction.

I illustrate on commission from my home studio and I'm pitching a children's book publisher. Here's the paragraph from my letter, wondering what you think.
"I draw the sort of picture a child finds on the third reading: the mouse behind the curtain, the half-eaten pear under the bed, the cat who looks guilty in every scene. My sketchbooks are full of these small secrets, and I would like to hide them in your books."

units: I'm a line cook turned kitchen manager, 31, working on my first startup. Pitch: "We give restaurants a free fryer-oil sensor that tells them the day the oil actually goes bad instead of the day the schedule says, and we take a cut of the oil they save." Does that come across clearly? Curious what you think.

I drive the Route 9 bus and write poems on my breaks. This is from the last run of the night. What do you think?
Route 9, final run. The bus exhales.
Rows of seats keep the shapes of strangers,
a dent here, a warmth there,
and I drive the empty ghosts back to the depot
with my headlights on for them.

I'm 22, bilingual, and I wrote this chorus about my mom making tortillas before work:
Mi mamá cuenta el mundo en tortillas
One for the rent, one for the rain
Dos para mí, y una para la esperanza
Flip it quick before it burns again
I'd really like to know what you think, especially about mixing the languages.

I'm 68 and retired, and I'm sick of mosquito-repelling phone apps. For my grandson's fair, we'll build a two-chamber choice box with a screen divider, put in 20 fruit flies, and then play the app's tone on only one side. A blinded helper chooses the side with a coin flip. After 10 minutes we count the flies per side. Then we'll repeat it 30 times and run a binomial test. What's your opinion?

I'm a financial adviser and I'm speaking to a room of twenty-somethings. I begin: "Imagine a stranger who will inherit everything you earn this year, and who currently receives none of it. He's you, at sixty-seven." How would you react to that if you were sitting in the audience?

I make a small podcast about local history from my closet, and I'm applying for a radio producer job. Here's the paragraph on my work. Can you tell me what you think?
"Episode 14 is eleven minutes about the 1952 flood, and nine of them are one woman, Dolores, describing the sound of the river at night. I cut my own questions to almost nothing. A producer's job, I've learned, is to build a quiet room and then leave it."

Flight instructor here, applying to a regional airline. This is the bullet I lead with: "Instructed 47 students to private pilot certificates with a 94% first-attempt checkride pass rate, versus a 71% national average." Curious how it reads to someone outside aviation. Thoughts?

Hey, this is from my intro DB class project (a book review site). I wanted the top 3 rated books in each category:
SELECT c.name AS category, t.title, t.rating
FROM categories c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT b.title, b.rating FROM books b
  WHERE b.category_id = c.id
  ORDER BY b.rating DESC, b.title
  LIMIT 3) t
ORDER BY c.name, t.rating DESC;
Would love to hear what you think!

Nursing student here, about to put this on my profile. Can you tell me what you think?
Good at: finding a vein first try, parallel parking, remembering your dog's name.
Working on: sourdough, leaving the group chat on read, believing me when I say "I'm fine."
Night rotations mean my weekends are Tuesdays. If you can be cheerful about dinner at 8 a.m., we'll get along.

I keep aquariums, and I'm trying duckweed as a nitrate sensor. I'll grow 10 fronds per jar in 0, 5, 20, and 50 ppm nitrate, then photograph from above every day for 12 days. ImageJ gives me the green area, which I'll use to calculate the growth rate. Three replicates, same light and temperature. Could I get your opinion on it?

units: I'm a school librarian and an immigrant, and I wrote this one for me too. Linh collects the wrong ways people say her name in jars: Lin, Lynn, Lean. Her grandmother says each jar is a small gift from someone who tried. On the last page, a new teacher asks Linh to say it first. I'd love your thoughts, truly.

Hello! This is my winter-interest border for Minnesota, 10x30 ft along the garage. Red twig dogwood at the back for stem colour against the snow. Mid layer: switchgrass 'Northwind' and sedum 'Matrona', both left standing. A paper birch cluster at the east end with white bark glowing at sunrise. Hellebores are tucked in near the door, so there's something to see on the shortest days. I'd like to know what you think!

I'm 55 and started saving late, so I'm catching up. Take-home $5,400: mortgage 1,450; groceries 500; utilities 280; car 350; health insurance 400; 401k catch-up 1,000; HSA 300; help with my son's college 500; fun 200; misc 420. Feeling a bit anxious about it. How does this look to you?

Sorry if this is a bit odd. I work in a post office sorting room and this came to me on shift. The start of my story:
"The dead letter office in Perth received, in 1962, a parcel containing forty-one left shoes. No note, no sender. Winifred Ames, who had spent nineteen years reuniting strangers with their mistakes, laid them in a row on the sorting table and felt, for the first time, outmatched."
What's your take?

I'm a mycology student making a logo for our research group. A mushroom is seen from underneath in a single deep brown, with its gills radiating out from the stem. The gills are drawn as fingerprint ridges, so the whole cap looks like a thumbprint. The group name is set in small capitals around the edge in a circle. How does it read to you?

I've been a carpenter for forty years and this is my first story. The narrator is a house. "The Pattersons took the couch, the lamps, and the cat. They left me the height marks on the kitchen doorframe, which I thought was kind." Then it waits for the next family. What's your take on it?

For my education course I wrote "Tuesday Is Late." Leo waits at the front door for Tuesday, because Mum said it was coming. Through the day the postman arrives, then rain, then Grandma with a bag of oranges. By dinner Leo decides Tuesday is made of all of them. I'm a bit worried about it being too quiet for a read-aloud. Can you give me your honest take?

Latest reading per sensor, for a dashboard that refreshes every few seconds. I'm an IoT hobbyist with a Raspberry Pi and a lot of sensors:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (sensor_id) sensor_id, recorded_at, temp_c
FROM readings
WHERE recorded_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
ORDER BY sensor_id, recorded_at DESC;
I also have an index on (sensor_id, recorded_at DESC). Any feedback would be great!

I keep bees, and I sell honey at the farmers' market, so I mapped a forage plan for my 1-acre lot. A six-foot hedge of serviceberry and pussy willow sits in front of the hives to force a high flight path. Bloom runs in order: willow in March, crocus, then lilac, then basswood, then borage and buckwheat in July. Asters and goldenrod go in for autumn. A shallow water dish with pebbles sits 10 ft from the hives. Does it look sensible?

I'm a product designer with 6 years of experience. Here's one bullet from my portfolio resume: "Redesigned insulin-pump onboarding after shadowing 18 patients at home; first-week setup errors dropped 46%, support calls fell by a third, and the app reached 4.7 stars." What's your reaction?

units:
Sorry if this is a bit odd. I work in a post office sorting room and this came to me on shift. The start of my story:
"The dead letter office in Perth received, in 1962, a parcel containing forty-one left shoes. No note, no sender. Winifred Ames, who had spent nineteen years reuniting strangers with their mistakes, laid them in a row on the sorting table and felt, for the first time, outmatched."
What's your take?
I'm a retired sailor who now makes waxed canvas bags. Slogan for the tag: "Carried through worse weather than this." I'd like to hear what you think.

My yarn budget is $50/month and I've got rules for it: $30 for yarn for projects already planned and charted, $10 for needles and notions, $5 for my local dyer's club, and $5 wildcard for anything that grabs me. If the wildcard isn't spent it carries over. Do you have any thoughts on it? I'm a little shy about sharing this!

I own a small bakery and write on slow afternoons. Here's how my short story opens: "The first thing my grandmother taught me about bread was that it lies. 'Dough tells you it's ready when it isn't,' she'd say, 'and tells you it's ruined when it's only shy.' She died in March. I have fed her starter every day since, though it has never once forgiven me for not being her." Honest thoughts?

Food truck owner here, and this is my salsa macha: toast 1 cup peanuts, 3 tbsp sesame seeds, and 6 chiles de árbol and 4 guajillos in 1 cup of neutral oil on low until fragrant and just darkening. Cool, then add 4 cloves roasted garlic, 1 tbsp piloncillo, 1 tsp dried orange peel, 1 tbsp cider vinegar and salt. Pulse it chunky. It goes on everything. Thoughts?

I'm a night-shift nurse and cook when I'm exhausted, so this is a one-pot dinner. Toast 2 tsp cumin seeds in olive oil, add onion, garlic, then 1½ cups red lentils and 6 cups water. Simmer 20 minutes. Stir in the chopped rind of half a preserved lemon, finish with lots of black pepper and a spoon of yogurt. Chili butter on top. Does this sound like something worth making again?

I'm nineteen and writing a dystopian novel for NaNoWriMo. It starts like this: "In the Ministry of Weather, I was the only person who knew it hadn't rained by itself in thirty years." Does it hook you? I'd really like an outside opinion.

I have ADHD and get bored by week two, so my plan has fixed anchors and random variety. Mon legs, Tue push, Thu pull, Sat carries and run. Each day's main lift never changes (squat, press, row, farmer carry). Accessories come from rolling a die against a list of six per day. Wed/Fri: 20-minute walk with podcasts. Sun: off. Tracking is one tick on the fridge. Do you think it holds together?

Hi! For my landscape studio course I designed a 12x20 ft Tucson courtyard. One desert willow in the northwest corner shades the hot afternoon wall. A dry-wash path of granite fines curves through brittlebush, Parry's penstemon and a single blue agave. A rain chain empties into a sunken basin planted with sedges. Seating sits on the east side for cool mornings. No turf. I present Thursday, so what's your take?

Ex-army, best man, and deadpan by nature. Draft: "I've served with Pete in two countries and one wedding rehearsal. Only the rehearsal made him sweat. Dani, I've watched this man wade into a flooded river to rescue a stranger's bag, and I've watched him cry at a dog food advert. He is brave for the right reasons and soft for the best ones. Look after both." How's the tone?

units: I'm a student and wrote a short poem for my Instagram, kind of nervous to ask but what do you think? "My grandmother counts in two languages: / Polish for coins and stairs, / English for the days since Dziadek, / and for the rosary, no language, / only the click of the next bead."

Hi! I'm 16 and I made these for my family's New Year dinner and I'm kind of nervous about sharing. Black sesame shortbread: 200g butter, 90g powdered sugar, 250g flour, 40g toasted ground black sesame, 1 tbsp orange zest, ½ tsp salt. Chill the dough 1 hour, slice, then roll the edges in raw sesame seeds. Bake at 160°C for 22 minutes. Could you tell me what you think?

Pascal's triangle as an infinite generator. I just love how the zip trick works out, and I'm a 52-year-old accountant who picked up Python during lockdown:
```python
def pascal():
    row = [1]
    while True:
        yield row
        row = [a + b for a, b in zip([0] + row, row + [0])]
```
What do you make of it?

Student cooking for my flatmates. My cacio e pepe variation: toast black pepper and 1 tsp red Sichuan peppercorns, crush coarsely. Cook 100g tonnarelli in very little water so the starch stays high, and pull it 2 minutes early. Off the heat, mix Pecorino with pasta water into a paste first, then toss everything together with the pepper. Can you give me feedback on the technique?

I'm a chef, and I wrote my best friend's wedding toast as a recipe. Ending: "Method: take two people who argue about salt. Add twelve years, one kitchen fire, and a very patient dog. Do not rush. Season with forgiveness, daily, to taste. Serves everyone at this table, who will leave fuller than they came. Tom, Maria: may you never run out." Honest thoughts?

Tonight I'm opening our astronomy club's star party. Here's the speech: "The light you'll see in Andromeda left 2.5 million years ago, before anything we'd call human. It has been traveling toward this field, this telescope, this paper cup of cocoa in your hand. Please don't rush. It's waited a long time for you. Red flashlights only, and be kind to the dark." What do you reckon?

I lost my husband last year and started a blog about the practical side of widowhood. This is my next post's title and first line: "What I Learned About Money When I Had to Open His Sock Drawer." "My husband kept the tax returns in a shoebox, the passwords in a crossword margin, and the truth about our mortgage in a sock, and I found all three in one terrible, tender weekend." How does it read to you?

I'm cataloguing my vinyl collection in Postgres with a tags array. Wanted live jazz albums but no Christmas ones:
CREATE INDEX albums_tags_gin ON albums USING gin (tags);
SELECT title, artist
FROM albums
WHERE tags @> ARRAY['jazz', 'live']
  AND NOT tags && ARRAY['christmas']
ORDER BY artist, title;
I'd love to know how this strikes you.

I'm a retired ferry captain turning a moored barge into a floating cafe. I'm naming it "Dead Reckoning," the old way of finding your position without landmarks, and now it's how I find my way into retirement. How does it strike you?

I've kept a sourdough starter for four years and decided to write about it. Thesis: "Pandemic sourdough was less a food trend than a time trend: a starter demands feeding on a schedule, and people locked at home wanted something that made the days measurably pass." Any reactions?

units: I'm a beekeeper with six hives, and I planned a 10m x 10m forage garden to support them from March to October. Early: crocus, willow, and hellebores. Spring: lungwort, borage, and fruit blossoms. Summer: lime tree, phacelia, and marjoram. Autumn: ivy, Sedum, and asters. Hives are in the southeast corner, facing away from the path, with a 2m hedge forcing bees to fly up. What do you think of it?

Our knitting group has two speeds: "I'll finish it by Christmas" and "Which Christmas?" I said that at last week's meetup and got a laugh, but I'm wondering whether it holds up written down. What do you think, any tweaks?

This is my first draft for an industrial design class assignment. "Halo Clip is a rear bike light that wraps around the seatpost and glows in a full ring, so drivers see you from the side as well as behind. USB-C charging, 12-hour runtime, and a silicone band that fits any post from 25 to 35 mm. At 41 grams, it weighs less than two AA batteries." Thoughts?

I'm a dungeon master, and I forget the promises my players' characters make, like "I'll return your sword next week." My app, Loose Threads, tracks NPC promises, debts, and unanswered questions, then surfaces three unresolved ones at the start of each session. You can tie each thread to a character. Thoughts? I'd like to know if other DMs would find it useful.

I keep bees, and I hate pulling off my gloves to take notes. My app is Hive Voice. During an inspection I say "Hive 4, queen seen, eggs yes, six frames of brood, a little crowded," and it fills in a structured log. It flags anything missing, like "No mention of mites." It also compares the entry with last month's. Is this something you could see helping people?

Mom of three, so my workouts ride on existing routines. Mon: while the pasta boils, 3 rounds of 10 squats and 10 counter push-ups. Tue: school-run walk, pushing the stroller up the big hill. Wed: during swim lessons, 30 laps. Thu: 20-minute kettlebell video while the kids watch a show. Fri: 15-minute kitchen dance party. Sat: family hike carrying the youngest. Sun: rest. Does this seem sustainable?

I spent twelve years as a paralegal and I'm opening a cafe across from the county courthouse. The name: "Grounds for Appeal." Lawyers and jurors will be my main customers. Does it work for you, or would you change anything?

the whole quad forgets its paths
until we make them.

units: Hi! I'm a line cook, six years in, applying for a sous chef job. Here's the middle paragraph of my letter: "At Marlow's I cut our walk-in waste from 14% to 5% by turning trim into the staff meal, then the staff meal into a Thursday special that outsold the ribeye. I'm not interested in cooking expensive food. I'm interested in making sure nothing that enters your kitchen dies in the bin." Honest thoughts?

Student cooking for my flatmates. My cacio e pepe variation: toast black pepper and 1 tsp red Sichuan peppercorns, crush coarsely. Cook 100g tonnarelli in very little water so the starch stays high, and pull it 2 minutes early. Off the heat, mix Pecorino with pasta water into a paste first, then toss everything together with the pepper. Can you give me feedback on the technique?

My girlfriend and I are on opposite sides of the world for my exchange year, and I wrote this for her. Would you tell me how it reads to you?
You're eating breakfast in my tomorrow.
I'm finishing your yesterday's dinner.
We pass the same hour
like two people
on a very long staircase.

Hi! I'm a pastry chef and I've been writing posts for my bakery's site. New one is called "Why Your Croissants Taste Like Bread With Ambitions." It opens: "Butter doesn't melt at 32°C so much as give up, and the exact moment it does is the whole reason your lamination collapses." Thoughts?

My little cousin stutters, and I wrote this for him. Caleb notices the river stutters too, tripping over every rock ("b-b-bubble, b-b-bubble"), yet it reaches the sea every single time. Nobody in the book ever says "fix." He just sits beside the water and talks back to it. I'm a bit nervous about getting it right. Would you mind giving me honest feedback?

I'm a first-generation college student writing a novel inspired by my family. Here's the opening line: "My mother carried two suitcases across the border: one for what we owned, and one, empty, for what we would be given." I'd be grateful to hear what you think of it.

I run a tiny bakery and I'm rewriting our menu. Here's the entry for our main loaf:
"Country loaf. 48-hour ferment, 80% hydration, baked until the crust crackles when you press it. Sour enough to wake you up, mild enough for a child's lunchbox. Best on day one, toasted on day three, croutons on day five. We bake 40 a morning; when they're gone, they're gone."
What's your opinion?

I own a small dumpling restaurant and I'm writing about my mum for the website. Title: "How to Fold a Dumpling Like My Mother Without Her Hands." First line: "My mother's hands folded eighteen pleats without looking, and after her stroke I had to learn to describe in words what her fingers had never needed to say." I'd be grateful to hear what you think.

I'm a mechanic, 52, and my daughter says I should show somebody this. So here goes. Tell me what you think.
Under the hood the engine's cooled to a tick,
a metal clock winding down its day.
I wipe my hands on a rag that's been
every color of every car I've loved.

Hi! I play chess competitively as a hobby, and I'm toasting two fellow club members. Here goes: "In chess, we say the opening is theory, the middlegame is imagination, and the endgame is technique. Raj and Claire skipped the opening, played a wildly imaginative middlegame in the club parking lot, and now they're in an endgame where the only rule is that nobody resigns. May every draw be by agreement. To Raj and Claire." Thoughts?

units:
First-gen student here. I wrote this hook after an internship interview and I'm kind of nervous to show anyone. What's your honest take?
Mama dusted the boardroom where I'm interviewing now,
she knew the table's every scar and never knew how
to ask for a seat there. So I'll sit, and I'll stay,
with her name in my mouth like the first thing I say.

I'm a night-shift nurse and cook when I'm exhausted, so this is a one-pot dinner. Toast 2 tsp cumin seeds in olive oil, add onion, garlic, then 1½ cups red lentils and 6 cups water. Simmer 20 minutes. Stir in the chopped rind of half a preserved lemon, finish with lots of black pepper and a spoon of yogurt. Chili butter on top. Does this sound like something worth making again?

I'm 24 and I've been a barista since I was 18. My pitch: "One loyalty card that works at every independent cafe in a neighborhood, funded by a 1% fee, so locals get their free tenth coffee and the chains' apps lose their advantage." Any thoughts? I haven't shown it to anyone yet.

Hi! I'm sending this to my manager at the coffee shop tomorrow. Here it is:
"Hi Dana, I have organic chemistry finals May 6 and 9, so I can't do my Thursday closes those weeks. Priya and Marcus both said they'd take them if I cover their Sunday opens on the 12th and 19th. I've already put the swaps in the shared sheet. If anything clashes, I'm happy to rework it. Thanks, Leo"
What do you think?

I run a bike repair shop and I'm finally writing for our website. Title: "Your Bike Isn't Making That Noise to Annoy You." Opening: "Every click, tick, and groan from a bicycle is a tiny confession, and after eleven years of fixing them above a laundromat, I can usually tell you what yours did last weekend before you finish describing the sound." Feedback welcome!

I drive long-haul and write these at truck stops. This one's from a night in Wyoming:
Wyoming, midnight—
my headlights find one fence post,
then lose it again
Curious what you think of it, especially the ending.

I do funeral photography and I'm starting a dark comedy. Logline: "A professional mourner who attends the funerals of the friendless finds herself at her estranged father's service, where no one else has shown up and her professional standards are on the line." Curious what you think!

I teach seventh grade and wrote this on the staffroom whiteboard today: "Teaching teenagers is like being a human Wi-Fi router: everyone's staring at me, nobody's connected, and the moment I move, they complain about the signal." Curious what people outside teaching make of it.

I'm the mayor of a town of 6,000 and I'm campaigning for the library levy. Here's a section of my speech: "A library is the last place in town where you can walk in with no money and nobody asks why you're there. It costs the average household $41 a year. Ask yourself what else you can buy that's open to everyone, including the person you'd never think of." How does that sit with you?

I'm a dog groomer and I've been wanting to write for my clients. Title: "Your Dog Is Not Afraid of the Bath." First sentence: "Most dogs I meet aren't afraid of water; they're afraid of slipping, and once you put down a rubber mat, the 'bath-hating' dog you've described for six years quietly disappears." What's your take?

units: I'm hiking Kilimanjaro in September and have 12 weeks. Mon: stair climb with a 10kg pack, 45 min. Tue: strength (step-ups, lunges, calf raises). Wed: rest. Thu: 5 miles easy with a pack. Fri: yoga for hips and breathing practice. Sat: 4-6 hour hike with elevation gain, adding an hour every two weeks. Sun: 40 min easy walk. I'll swap in a sauna session twice weekly for heat. Opinions welcome!

I'm 14 and I like music, so I'm doing Chladni plates. I'm bolting a 20 cm square aluminum plate to a speaker driver, sprinkling salt on it, and sweeping frequencies from 100 to 3000 Hz. I'll photograph each pattern at resonance, then compare the frequencies to the theoretical plate-mode formula to find which ones match. I'll also test how the patterns change when I clamp the plate at its center vs. its edge. What do you think?

Stand-up comic, 26, and I finally wrote a bio I'm ready to post. "I'm funnier in person, which is the worst thing a comedian can put on a dating app. Five-six, or six if the shoes are loud. I will make a joke about our first fight during our first fight. Looking for someone who can take a punchline and deliver a better one." Be honest!

I design board games as a hobby and I'm giving a talk at a small convention. I'm opening with: "The most important rule in my game is on the back of the box, in small type: 'The player who is winning may not know it.'" What's your opinion?

Hobbyist beekeeper here. Our club's oldest member, Arlo, is hanging up his veil. My toast: "Arlo told me bees don't care about your day. Move slow, breathe, and they'll let you in. I've tried to live that way since. Sixty years, millions of bees, and only eleven stings, he claims. Arlo, you kept the hives and the humans calm. We'll leave the smoker lit for you." Do you think it works?

I'm a line cook who got curious about browning. I'll caramelize identical onion slices in solutions of baking soda at five different pH levels, then photograph each batch every 5 minutes next to a gray card and convert the pixels to L*a*b* color values. Then I'll plot how fast browning happens against pH. I'm a little nervous presenting at a science fair as a non-scientist. What do you think of it?
I'm a dog walker and I'm putting together business cards. The slogan I wrote is "Tired dogs, happy couches." Can you tell me what you think? I'm a bit nervous about showing it to anyone.

I've been given the lease on a lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Northumberland coast, and I'm turning it into a cafe. The name is "Last Light." We'll close at dusk, so you can watch the lamp come on while you finish your tea. I'm 62 and a bit sentimental about it. What's your reaction to the name?

I'm a software engineer and I've planned a 5m x 7m garden inspired by Japanese design, but adapted to Ohio. The idea: three clustered stones in an area of raked gravel, shaped like a dry stream. It's crossed by a flat stone bridge. A Japanese maple stands in the corner, and I've placed moss under a shaded eave. I'm keeping the plant list to nine species, and nothing is symmetrical. Here's the plan. What do you think?

I'm 11 and my idea for an app is called Pet Shift. My family has one dog and four people, and he keeps getting fed twice. You tap "Fed Biscuit" once. If someone else tries to tap it within two hours, the phone says "Dad already fed Biscuit 12 minutes ago." Then it shows a picture of Biscuit looking guilty. What do you think? My mom said to ask someone who knows apps.

WITH r AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(revenue) AS rev FROM sales GROUP BY product_id)

def merge(intervals):
    out = []
    for lo, hi in sorted(intervals):
        if out and lo <= out[-1][1]:
            out[-1][1] = max(out[-1][1], hi)
        else:
            out.append([lo, hi])
    return out
```

I'm a fire captain, not a writer, and I said this for Lou, retiring after 30 years: 'Lou taught me the most important rule of the job: you can be the bravest person in the building, but you still wash your own dishes. Photography is my hobby, and I'm selling prints for the first time. Here's my listing text: "Fog at Pigeon Point, 12x18 archival pigment print on cotton rag paper. Shot at 5:40 a.m., it holds seven shades of grey between the lighthouse and the sea. Signed, numbered, edition of 50. Ships flat in a rigid mailer, with a card telling you where I stood." Feedback welcome.

"Among night-shift med-surg nurses, does a protected 20-minute nap at 3 a.m. reduce medication-administration near-misses in the final three hours of the shift, compared with no scheduled break?" Could you give me your honest opinion? I'm a little nervous about it.

WHERE o.payload ? 'items';

What do you think?

My loaf: 500g bread flour, 100g whole wheat, 20g toasted barley flour, with cold roasted barley tea replacing the water (80% hydration). 20% levain, four stretch-and-folds, overnight cold proof, baked covered at 245°C for 20 minutes, then uncovered for 22. Does the formula make sense to you? Any tweaks you'd suggest?

I'm a second-year econ PhD student trying to write for a general audience. Title: "The Bus Fare Is a Lie We Agreed On." Opening: "Every city bus fare is a price set not by what a ride costs but by what a mayor can survive charging, which makes the fare box less a cash register than a weekly opinion poll." Does it work for you?

Monthly cohort retention for our subscription app. I'm a data scientist and wrote it in one sitting, so tell me if I've missed something.
WITH f AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(date_trunc('month', ordered_at)) AS cohort
  FROM orders GROUP BY 1)
SELECT f.cohort,
  DATEDIFF('month', f.cohort, date_trunc('month', o.ordered_at)) AS months_since,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS active
FROM f JOIN orders o USING (customer_id)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

I own a small bakery and I'm writing a post to explain our prices. Title: "Why Our Croissants Cost $4.50." First sentence: "A croissant is three days of waiting disguised as breakfast: one day for the dough, one for the butter to settle into it, and one for me to stop touching it." Could you tell me your impressions?

Monthly cohort retention for our subscription app. I'm a data scientist and wrote it in one sitting, so tell me if I've missed something.
WITH f AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(date_trunc('month', ordered_at)) AS cohort
  FROM orders GROUP BY 1)
SELECT f.cohort,
  DATEDIFF('month', f.cohort, date_trunc('month', o.ordered_at)) AS months_since,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS active
FROM f JOIN orders o USING (customer_id)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;
</message>

units: I'm a 911 dispatcher, 48. Here's what I said at Carla's last-shift party: 'Carla has been the first voice on the worst day of ten thousand lives. She never got to see how any of them ended. A wildflower meadow, mown only in September, surrounds it, with a hedgerow of hawthorn, blackthorn, and dog rose on the windward side. A log pile and a stone hibernaculum for amphibians sits at the east end. Do you have any feedback?

Bootcamp student here. I needed to turn nested config into flat keys and ended up with this recursive version. How would you rate it?
```js
const flat = (o, p = '') =>
  Object.entries(o).flatMap(([k, v]) =>
    v && typeof v === 'object' ? flat(v, p + k + '.') : [[p + k, v]]);
Object.fromEntries(flat({ a: { b: 1, c: { d: 2 } } }));
```

I'm 68 and want my clubhead speed back. Mon/Thu: cable chops, 3 kg medicine-ball rotational throws against a wall 3x8, goblet squats. Tue/Fri: walk 5 km, carrying my bag. Wed: 20 minutes of hip and thoracic mobility. Sat: golf. Sun: rest. I'm tracking my driver speed on the range once a month. Does this look reasonable to you?

I taught fourth grade for 34 years and I'm applying to be a docent at the natural history museum. The questions they asked in that silence taught me more about teaching than any training did. I'd like to bring that minute of silence to your visitors." Could you tell me what you make of it?

Thu: cable hose-pull simulation 5x30 s, dummy drags. Fri: heavy deadlifts 5x3. Sat: full timed test circuit. Sun: rest, foam roll. Does this seem right to you?

My small city yard is 15x30 ft, so I made a four-bed rotation plan: Bed A brassicas, Bed B legumes and peas, Bed C tomatoes, peppers and basil, Bed D roots and alliums. Each moves one bed clockwise every year, and compost goes on whichever bed is next to host the tomatoes. Cover crop of crimson clover fills any gap in winter. A 2 ft path loop keeps everything within arm's reach. Opinions?

async function retry(fn, { tries = 5, base = 100 } = {}) {
  for (let i = 0; ; i++) {
    try { return await fn(i); }
    catch (e) {
      if (i + 1 >= tries) throw e;

}
