units: I'm a chef, and I wrote my best friend's wedding toast as a recipe. Ending: "Method: take two people who argue about salt. Add twelve years, one kitchen fire, and a very patient dog. Do not rush. Season with forgiveness, daily, to taste. Serves everyone at this table, who will leave fuller than they came. Tom, Maria: may you never run out." Honest thoughts?

I teach physics and wrote this over the holidays. Opening paragraph:
"The last astronomer on Earth kept her telescope pointed at the same dead star for forty years, not because she expected it to change but because someone had to be there for the nothing. Her grandson thought this was sad. She thought it was the only job left that was entirely honest."
I'd love to hear what you think.

I run a little hardware store and wrote a rhyming book. Here's how it opens:
"When the owner turns the sign and the keys click twice,
the hammers call to order and the washers roll dice;
the tape measures argue about who's most long,
and the level says, 'Friends, you are all slightly wrong.'"
What do you think? I'm curious whether the rhythm holds up when read aloud.

Hi! I'm 16 and I made these for my family's New Year dinner and I'm kind of nervous about sharing. Black sesame shortbread: 200g butter, 90g powdered sugar, 250g flour, 40g toasted ground black sesame, 1 tbsp orange zest, ½ tsp salt. Chill the dough 1 hour, slice, then roll the edges in raw sesame seeds. Bake at 160°C for 22 minutes. Could you tell me what you think?

I roast coffee out of my garage and I'm calling the brand Second Crack. The logo is a single coffee bean, top-down, in matte black. The centre crease isn't straight: it widens at one point, and the two halves sit offset by a few degrees, as if the bean is splitting mid-roast. Nothing else, no text in the mark. What's your opinion?

Here's my hellstrip plan, 8x25 ft, Ontario zone 5, casual and just for fun. Three height bands. Front: prairie dropseed at 18 in spacing, so it reads tidy to neighbours. Middle: golden alexanders, then pale purple coneflower, then anise hyssop for a May to September bloom run. Back: New England aster and little bluestem for October colour. Seedheads stay up until March for the finches. What would you change, if anything?

I'm in 6th grade and I'm testing paper airplane winglets. I made a launcher from a ruler and a rubber band pulled back to exactly 10 cm so every launch has the same speed. I'll fold 5 identical planes for each wing design (none, up, down, and split tips), throw each one 10 times, and record the glide distance from a fixed height. Then I'll calculate the glide ratio for each. Does this sound good to you?

I'm a farmer, new to writing. In the town of Marl, your umbrella opens onto whatever you're feeling: Grandpa's makes drizzle, the mayor's makes hail. Nell's opens only sunshine, because she never lets anyone see her sad. The day it finally drizzles over her, the whole town comes to stand underneath. Tell me what you think, please.

I'm a retired electrician, 68, starting a blog. Title: "The Last Man in Ohio Who Still Respects Knob-and-Tube Wiring." First sentence: "In 1931 somebody in Zanesville ran two wires through a wall using porcelain tubes and a prayer, and I have spent forty years learning to respect that prayer." Be straight with me, what's your honest reaction?

I'm a hobbyist game designer. Memory-care homes seem to run on bingo, so I made a kit: large tiles with photos of 1950s kitchen objects that residents match and talk about, plus a facilitator card with three open questions. $65 per kit. One activity director tried it, and residents were still chatting after 40 minutes. I'd like to sell it to care homes. What's your take?

```python
from datetime import timedelta
def add_business_days(start, n, holidays=frozenset()):
    step = 1 if n >= 0 else -1
    d = start
    while n:
        d += timedelta(days=step)
        if d.weekday() < 5 and d not in holidays:
            n -= step
    return d
```

I'm happy to take criticism.

Retired DBA here, tinkering for fun. I wrote an org chart query for our club's volunteer table. Cycle guard included, since people enter data badly:
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
  SELECT id, name, manager_id, name::text AS path, 0 AS depth FROM staff WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, c.path || ' > ' || e.name, c.depth + 1
  FROM staff e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id WHERE c.depth < 12)
SELECT * FROM chain ORDER BY path;
What's your opinion?

I garden on an allotment and wrote this to decide whether to water, with recent rain counting for more. Rough hobby code, but I'd like an opinion:
```python
def needs_water(rain_mm, threshold=15, decay=0.7):
    """rain_mm is oldest-first, one value per day."""
    effective = sum(mm * decay**age
                    for age, mm in enumerate(reversed(rain_mm)))
    return effective < threshold
```

units: I'm a hospice social worker, and this has stayed with me for years. "We pair hospice patients with trained oral-history students who record a 90-minute interview, cut it into a 12-minute film, and deliver it to the family within a week, paid for from the hospice's bereavement budget." What's your reaction?

I'm a marine engineer starting a sailboat rigging business, Bowline Marine. The mark is a rope tied in a bowline, drawn as one thick line in navy. The loop of the knot forms the bowl of a capital B, and the standing part runs down as its stem. The working end of the rope tucks behind, and you can follow the knot correctly. Does it hold up, in your view?

I'm a school librarian and an immigrant, and I wrote this one for me too. Linh collects the wrong ways people say her name in jars: Lin, Lynn, Lean. Her grandmother says each jar is a small gift from someone who tried. On the last page, a new teacher asks Linh to say it first. I'd love your thoughts, truly.

I drive the 14 bus and I've been invited to speak to the city council about route cuts. I've never done this before. I'm going to start with: "I drive the 14 bus, which means I've watched this city wake up four thousand times, and I can tell you exactly where it's tired." What do you think?

I'm 67 and marrying for the second time, after being widowed. My toast: "Thirty years ago I promised someone forever and meant it. Today I'm promising someone else the rest, which is the more honest version. Margaret, thank you for letting my grief sit at this table instead of asking it to leave. To those who aren't here, and to those who are." Does it feel right to you?

I'm new to selling tea and a little nervous. Here's the description I wrote for one of my teas:
"Lapsang Souchong, smoked over pine. A campfire in a cold cabin: resinous, faintly sweet, with a surprising hint of dried longan on the finish. Steep at 95°C for three minutes. Try it with salty cheese, or with rain."
Could you tell me how it reads?

I knit as a hobby and I've been toying with a business idea. One sentence: "Knitters abandon sweaters at the sleeves because patterns don't fit their bodies, so we sell $14 pattern files that recalculate every stitch count from five measurements." Curious what you make of it, be as blunt as you like!

I'm a weekend woodworker selling at a craft fair, and this is my sign copy. "End-grain walnut and maple board, 14 x 10 inches. Knife edges sink between the fibers and the grain closes behind them, so your blades stay sharper and the board shows fewer scars. Finished with mineral oil and beeswax. About six pounds, heavy enough to stay put while you chop." Any thoughts?

I live on a steep slope in Cape Town, and this is my plan for terraced fynbos. Four dry-stone terraces, each 1.5m wide, with the steps offset so water never funnels down. Top terrace: proteas and leucadendrons. Middle: restios and pelargoniums. Bottom: Agapanthus and buchu near the path. No irrigation after the first summer. I'd really love your feedback on the plan!

Here's my idea: erosion control. I build four 30° slopes in trays: bare soil, grass, mulch, and gravel. A watering can with 100 drilled holes simulates 20 minutes of steady rain from a fixed height. I collect the runoff and dry it to find the sediment mass, and I measure the total water volume too. Three replicates per cover. What do you think?

```python
def primes_up_to(n):
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:

    return [i for i, p in enumerate(sieve) if p]
```

I'm a sysadmin and I've been burned by half-written config files, so I made this:
```python
def atomic_write(path, data):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
            f.write(data)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        os.unlink(tmp)
        raise
```
What's your opinion?

How does that sound to you?

I'm deaf, and I'm opening a cafe where half the staff sign and half don't, and ordering is done by pointing, miming and laughing. I'm calling it "Handful." It's a handful of beans, and it's a hand you can talk with. I'm 24 and this is my first business. What do you reckon of the name?

I've been home with my kids for 8 years and I'm applying for a project coordinator job. Nervous! Paragraph: "For eight years I've managed a team of three with unpredictable deadlines, no budget, and a 6 a.m. launch every day. I also ran the school auction, which raised $41,000 using one spreadsheet and fifty unreliable volunteers. People call that a transferable skill. I'd like to prove it on yours." Honest reaction, please?

I'm a herbalist who wants to build a 6m x 6m tea and medicine garden. It's a mandala, with four quadrants divided by paths: calming (chamomile, lemon balm, lavender), digestive (peppermint, fennel, calendula), immune (echinacea, elderberry, thyme), and a quadrant for rotating annuals. In the center, a small sundial surrounded by holy basil. Drying racks are on the shed's south wall. What do you make of it?

Weekend gardener here, and my zucchini has gotten completely out of hand. I turned it into a country chorus. Be straight with me, what's your take?
Zucchini in July, please, I'm begging you stop,
I've left bags on porches, I've filled the church shop.
The neighbors all wave with a too-careful smile.
They've seen me coming up the drive for a mile.

I teach pottery classes as a hobby, and I'm designing a project on crazing. Same clay body and same glaze on 18 tiles. I fire them together, then cool them at three rates by cracking the kiln lid at 900°C, 700°C, or leaving it closed. I count crazing lines per cm² after 24 hours and a week. What would you say about this?

Self-employed plumber, three kids. I pay myself $6,000 a month from the business. Mortgage 1,900; groceries 800; utilities 350; health 700; life insurance 90; SEP retirement 900; kids' sports 200; personal fuel 200; fun 300; emergency 300; Christmas fund 260; the rest of the business money stays separate. Be straight with me. What do you reckon?

Powerlifting hobbyist, meet is in 8 days. Mon: squat 3x2 at 85%, bench 3x3 at 80%. Tue: rest. Wed: deadlift 2x2 at 85%, easy accessory work. Thu: bench singles up to 90%, short walk. Fri: rest. Sat: openers only, 30 min mobility. Sun: travel, light food, sleep. Volume drops about 40% while intensity stays high. Would love a second pair of eyes on this taper.
Hi! I'm 19 and just launched a tiny Etsy shop selling hand-knitted wool socks. My slogan: "Socks that make winter a rumour." Would love to hear what you think, even if it's blunt.

Shared this on Instagram with a photo from my old Olympus: "Shot on a 1974 camera I bought for $20. The light leak in the corner was an accident. My grandfather's hand in the frame wasn't: he was waving me off, and I'm glad I pressed the shutter anyway." Could you tell me what you make of it?

units: I'm part of our college radio station and we're redoing the logo. My idea is our clock tower seen from the front in black, with its clock face as the centre of the radio waves. Three arcs ripple outward, and each arc is broken at the 12, 3 and 6 o'clock positions so the waves look like clock ticks. Thoughts?

I make a true crime podcast about small towns, called Dead Air. The logo is an audio waveform running across the width of the square. The peaks on the left are shaped like rooftops, a steeple, a water tower, a gabled barn, and then the line goes completely flat for the right third. White on charcoal. I'm a bit nervous posting this. How does it read to you?

Hi! I'm a junior developer and I made this joke after a rough week of code reviews: "My last pull request got the feedback 'LGTM.' I've since learned that's Latin for 'I did not open the file.'" I'm thinking of posting it on our team Slack. What's your take?

I'm 24 and I've been a barista since I was 18. My pitch: "One loyalty card that works at every independent cafe in a neighborhood, funded by a 1% fee, so locals get their free tenth coffee and the chains' apps lose their advantage." Any thoughts? I haven't shown it to anyone yet.

I'm a student who works at a skate rink, and I spotted a hazard. This is my email to my manager:
"Hi Joan, the rubber mat by the rental counter has curled at one corner. Two kids tripped on it today, and nobody was hurt. I've put an orange cone on it and taken a photo, attached. A replacement is about $40 at the hardware store on Elm, and I can pick it up on my way in tomorrow. Okay to do that? Thanks, Sam"
What do you think?

I'm a beekeeper with six hives, and I planned a 10m x 10m forage garden to support them from March to October. Early: crocus, willow, and hellebores. Spring: lungwort, borage, and fruit blossoms. Summer: lime tree, phacelia, and marjoram. Autumn: ivy, Sedum, and asters. Hives are in the southeast corner, facing away from the path, with a 2m hedge forcing bees to fly up. What do you think of it?

Casual dinner-party starter I came up with. Whole carrots tossed in olive oil, honey and smoked paprika, roasted at 220°C for 30 minutes. Serve on whipped labneh with lemon zest and garlic, scatter with homemade dukkah (hazelnut, coriander, sesame, cumin), and finish with hot honey spiked with sherry vinegar. Would this work as a starter, or is it too much going on?

We're farmers and just started jarring pickles. My wife says I should ask strangers what they think. Here's the label text:
"Dill spears from our back field, picked at breakfast, jarred by lunch. Garlic, dill heads, sea salt, and a grape leaf to keep them crunchy. No sugar, no vinegar, just a warm week on the counter. Open one on a hot day. Once opened, they keep two months in the fridge, though they rarely last a week."

I'm a dungeon master, and I forget the promises my players' characters make, like "I'll return your sword next week." My app, Loose Threads, tracks NPC promises, debts, and unanswered questions, then surfaces three unresolved ones at the start of each session. You can tie each thread to a character. Thoughts? I'd like to know if other DMs would find it useful.

```js
  take: n => lazy((function* () {
    if (n <= 0) return;
```

units: I'm an urban planning student and I write a commuter blog. Title: "Mapping the Number 9 Bus." First sentence: "The 9 crosses eleven neighborhoods in forty minutes, which means that every morning I travel through three tax brackets, two languages, and one very opinionated pigeon." Okay, be honest: what's your reaction to this?

I track my D&D group's attendance. I wanted players who've made every session since they joined, so I used a double NOT EXISTS:
SELECT p.name
FROM players p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM sessions s
  WHERE s.played_on >= p.joined_on
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM attendance a
      WHERE a.session_id = s.id AND a.player_id = p.id));
This is my first time trying that. Does it work for you?

I'm a court stenographer who writes thrillers on the side, and I've been sitting on this logline for months. "A court stenographer realizes the defendant's testimony matches, word for word, the transcript of a trial that has not happened yet." Could you give me your opinion?

I'm a freelance translator and I've made a joke about my marriage: "Being married to a translator means every argument ends with 'Well, that's not what the original said.'" My husband has asked me not to put it in my newsletter. Do you think I should?

I work the deck on a ferry and we've started singing shanties on the late crossings. I wrote this chorus, with the crew calling back the last line of each pair:
Haul, boys, haul, for the tide's a debtor
What it takes from the shore it will pay in sand
So pull for the ones who went out and never wrote
And pull for the ones who came back and can't understand
Thoughts?
Hi, I do freelance branding and I'm sharing a line for an umbrella brand that sells to windy coastal towns: "Built for the wind that ruins other umbrellas." What's your take?

I'm a weekend woodworker. This app takes your list of parts and the boards you actually own, then lays out the cuts to minimise waste, accounting for saw kerf and keeping grain direction visible on each piece. You'd get a printable diagram for each board. I'd love an honest reaction, since I mostly just use it on my own projects.

I'm a high school senior applying for a front-desk job at a vet clinic. Here's my paragraph, and I'd like to know your opinion, even if it's blunt.
"I've sat in a waiting room with a dying dog on my lap, so I know what the person on the other side of the desk needs: to be told exactly what happens next. I'm good with forms and phones. But I'm best at saying, quietly, 'Take all the time you need.'"

I moved here from Vietnam eight years ago. My idea is Backpack Letter. You photograph any school letter or form. It tells you in Vietnamese, or another language you choose, what the letter is about, what you have to do, and the deadline. Then it adds the deadline to your calendar, with a reminder two days before. It never translates word for word. It says things like "They need a signature, not money." I'd like your opinion.

I'm a drummer and teacher. My app is Ghost Bars, a metronome that goes silent. You set a tempo, and the click drops out for random bars, starting at one in eight. As you stay steady, it slowly increases the share of silent bars. When the click returns, it shows in milliseconds how far you drifted. It's meant to train internal pulse instead of leaning on the click. Does it seem worthwhile?

units: I run a small bike repair shop and I'm writing a piece for our city's business blog. Thesis: "Right-to-repair laws are usually defended on economic grounds, but their strongest case is epistemic: a society that can't open its devices gradually loses the ability to understand the things it depends on." Thoughts?

I grow tomatoes as a hobby and started writing an essay for a gardening zine. Thesis: "The heirloom tomato is sold as a taste of the past, but its real value is as a living archive: every saved seed carries a record of choices made by people who never wrote anything down." Curious what you think!

I teach kindergarten and my class asked where puddles go. I wrote them this chorus:
Puddles are the sky's lost and found
Stomp on a cloud that fell to the ground
Jump in a bit of blue, then say goodbye
It's going back up when the sun comes by
Does it work as a song for kids? Any thoughts appreciated!

I've dispatched for a regional trucking company for eight years and want to move into logistics analysis. Here's my bullet: "Rerouted a 40-truck fleet using a weather- and traffic-weighted spreadsheet model I built, cutting deadhead miles 17% and saving about 31,000 gallons of diesel per year." Mind giving me your opinion?

I'm a hobbyist and I'm trying out dew collection. Four 20 × 20 cm panels (aluminium, painted aluminium, plastic, and cotton) are set up on my roof at 30° overnight, and I weigh the water collected each dawn. I'm logging humidity, temperature, and sky cover, so I can compare conditions across 20 nights. Could you tell me your thoughts?

I groom dogs for a living and wanted my bio to be a little different. Could I get your thoughts?
"I spend my days making nervous dogs feel brave. I'm not saying I can do the same for you, but I'm not not saying it. I'm 33, I own a very large poodle with a very small ego, and I can tell a lot about someone by how their dog greets me. No dog? No problem, I'll take your word."

I'm an urban planner and I wrote this on the train. Ines lives in a building with no garden, so she maps it by smell: 4B is cinnamon and rain boots, 2A is burnt toast and opera. Mr. Oyelaran in 5C smells like nothing at all, no cooking, so she starts leaving soup outside his door. What do you make of it?

My project: how does plate thickness affect Chladni patterns? I'll vibrate square aluminium plates (1, 1.5, 2 mm) with a speaker driver and sweep frequency until sand forms the same mode shape. Theory predicts frequency scales with thickness, so I'll plot f against t and see how close my data comes. I'll photograph each pattern. Does this seem like a good plan to you?

I coach marathoners. My app is called Negative Split. Most pacing apps talk constantly, which drives me nuts. This one stays silent while you're within 5 seconds per mile of target. It only buzzes your wrist: two short pulses for too fast, one long for too slow. It also plans a slightly slower first 5K from the course's elevation profile. Can you give me feedback?

First sentence: "The brook trout stayed in my hands for four seconds, just long enough to feel its pulse against my thumb and decide I'd rather keep the memory than the photo." Wondering how this strikes you as a reader.

"Hi Paula, closing takes us 55 minutes because we sweep each theater after cleaning the concession counter. If one person starts on the theaters while the other counts the till, I timed it at 35 minutes in a trial last Friday. What do you think?

"I'm a 5.10 climber with a 5.13 vocabulary for complaining about it. Strong opinions: chalk bags should be washed, belay attention should be absolute, and the best part of any route is the sitting-down afterward. Looking for a partner who'll catch my falls and my terrible puns, in that order."

I'm a medical interpreter and need to update my resume. Here's the bullet I'm working with: "Interpreted live for 300+ oncology consults in Mandarin and Cantonese; led creation of an 85-term bilingual glossary now used by the hospital's entire language services department." Does it work for you?

I'll photograph each pattern at resonance, then compare the frequencies to the theoretical plate-mode formula to find which ones match. I'll also test how the patterns change when I clamp the plate at its center vs. its edge. What do you think?

Environmental science major here. My thesis for the policy paper: "Carbon offsets fail not because forests burn but because they sell a permanent license for a temporary promise: a ton emitted today stays in the atmosphere for centuries, while the tree that 'cancels' it can be cut down next decade." Thoughts?

I knit and sell sweaters, and I wrote this to work out cast-on counts from my gauge. What's your opinion?
```python
def cast_on(width_cm, stitches_per_10cm, repeat=4, edge=2):
    """Round to the nearest pattern repeat, then add edge stitches."""
    raw = width_cm * stitches_per_10cm / 10
    return round(raw / repeat) * repeat + edge
```

units: I live on a steep slope in Cape Town, and this is my plan for terraced fynbos. Four dry-stone terraces, each 1.5m wide, with the steps offset so water never funnels down. Top terrace: proteas and leucadendrons. Middle: restios and pelargoniums. Bottom: Agapanthus and buchu near the path. No irrigation after the first summer. I'd really love your feedback on the plan!

I'm an urban planner with an idea called Desire Lines. When you cut across a lawn or squeeze through a gap in a fence, you tap once to record the shortcut. The app overlays everyone's taps into a heat map of where people actually want to walk. Cities could use it to put paths where feet already go. I'd really like your thoughts.

Latest reading per sensor, for a dashboard that refreshes every few seconds. I'm an IoT hobbyist with a Raspberry Pi and a lot of sensors:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (sensor_id) sensor_id, recorded_at, temp_c
FROM readings
WHERE recorded_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
ORDER BY sensor_id, recorded_at DESC;
I also have an index on (sensor_id, recorded_at DESC). Any feedback would be great!

I drive the night bus on the number 14 route. I've been jotting haiku on my break for years. Here's one I finally typed up:
Last bus, rain-streaked glass—
each passenger's face lit once
by passing streetlights
What would you say about it?

I'm a weekend birder writing to save a patch of wetland from development. Opening: "A blackpoll warbler weighs less than a AA battery and crosses an ocean to reach our marsh every autumn. The least we can do is leave the marsh where it left it." Not sure how to follow that up, but what do you think of the start?

Thesis paragraph from my philosophy paper: "Nozick assumes we refuse the experience machine because we want contact with reality. I think we refuse because we want to be answerable: to be the kind of person who can let someone down. A simulated life contains no one we can fail, and so no one whose forgiveness we can earn. That, not the missing real world, is what we'd mourn." Does the argument hold together?

I run a small bike repair shop and I'm writing a piece for our city's business blog. Thesis: "Right-to-repair laws are usually defended on economic grounds, but their strongest case is epistemic: a society that can't open its devices gradually loses the ability to understand the things it depends on." Thoughts?
I make alarm clocks, small batch, with a sunrise light. The line I'm testing for the box is: "Gentle enough to forgive you. Loud enough not to." What do you think?

units: Casual dinner-party starter I came up with. Whole carrots tossed in olive oil, honey and smoked paprika, roasted at 220°C for 30 minutes. Serve on whipped labneh with lemon zest and garlic, scatter with homemade dukkah (hazelnut, coriander, sesame, cumin), and finish with hot honey spiked with sherry vinegar. Would this work as a starter, or is it too much going on?

I've been a grant writer for 12 years and I'm trying something looser for our food bank's donor letter. "Dear Ms. Alvarez, Last Tuesday a man in our line held up a can of chickpeas and asked if it was for people or for the cat. I said people. He said, 'Good. Then I'll take two.' Hunger here isn't dramatic. It's arithmetic." Thoughts?

I illustrate on commission from my home studio and I'm pitching a children's book publisher. Here's the paragraph from my letter, wondering what you think.
"I draw the sort of picture a child finds on the third reading: the mouse behind the curtain, the half-eaten pear under the bed, the cat who looks guilty in every scene. My sketchbooks are full of these small secrets, and I would like to hide them in your books."

I'm a planetary scientist and I wrote a comic sci-fi novel for fun. The opening line: "Technically, I am the last human on Mars, but the robots have been very nice about it." My friends laughed, but they're my friends. What's your opinion?

I'm a financial adviser and I'm speaking to a room of twenty-somethings. I begin: "Imagine a stranger who will inherit everything you earn this year, and who currently receives none of it. He's you, at sixty-seven." How would you react to that if you were sitting in the audience?

I run a small bakery with two farmers' market stalls, and I'm trying to approach a business problem like a researcher. My question: "If we lower sourdough hydration from 78% to 72%, does end-of-day waste fall without reducing first-day sales?" I'd test it over eight Saturdays, alternating stalls. Tell me what you make of it.

I run a pet-sitting business and I'm emailing the manager of the kennel I partner with. Here goes:
"Hi Greta, over July 4th weekend, I'd like to reserve five overflow kennels for my regular clients. All five dogs are vaccinated, and I'll send their records by Friday. I'll drop off, feed, and walk them myself, so there's no extra work for your staff. I can pay $200 up front. Could you confirm by the 20th? Thanks, Marcus"
What do you think?

I'm a weekend woodworker and I'm demoing at our makerspace open house. I'm opening with: "This chair has no screws, no nails, and no glue. It's held together by nothing but the fact that wood shrinks." Just wondering how that sounds to you. Be as blunt as you like!

units:
I've been struggling and finally wrote this to my manager. I'm nervous. Can you tell me how it reads?
"Hi Lena, I need to be upfront: I've been running on empty since the audit and my work is slipping. I'd like to take the five leave days I have left next week, then talk about moving the Q3 report to someone else. I'd rather tell you now than miss it."

I'm a Dungeon Master and posted this on r/DnD: "My players found a door that only opened if you told it the truth. Three hours later the paladin admitted he'd never liked his god, and the door was still locked. It was waiting for the rogue." Does it land for you?

I'm a paralegal who writes at lunch. Here's the first line of my chapter book: "The day Marguerite Okonkwo-Bell turned nine, she inherited a lighthouse, a debt, and a very opinionated seagull." The seagull has strong views on her accounting. I'm wondering what you'd say about the voice and where it might go.

Hobby beekeeper here, and I'm a little proud of this one. I'd lease rooftop hives to restaurants for $85 a month. I handle all inspections, and they get 20 jars a year labelled with their street name, plus a QR code to a short video of 'their' bees. Chefs get a menu story, and I fund my other 12 hives. Three owners have said they're interested. Does it seem worth pursuing?

I keep aquariums, and I'm trying duckweed as a nitrate sensor. I'll grow 10 fronds per jar in 0, 5, 20, and 50 ppm nitrate, then photograph from above every day for 12 days. ImageJ gives me the green area, which I'll use to calculate the growth rate. Three replicates, same light and temperature. Could I get your opinion on it?

I'm a college sophomore starting a laundry fund for students who can't afford the machines. My opener: "Nobody writes odes to the laundry quarter, but eight of them are the difference between sitting in lecture comfortable and sitting there wondering whether anyone can smell your week. We'd like to make that difference free." Opinion?

I'm 11 and my idea for an app is called Pet Shift. My family has one dog and four people, and he keeps getting fed twice. You tap "Fed Biscuit" once. If someone else tries to tap it within two hours, the phone says "Dad already fed Biscuit 12 minutes ago." Then it shows a picture of Biscuit looking guilty. What do you think? My mom said to ask someone who knows apps.

I'm a drummer and teacher. My app is Ghost Bars, a metronome that goes silent. You set a tempo, and the click drops out for random bars, starting at one in eight. As you stay steady, it slowly increases the share of silent bars. When the click returns, it shows in milliseconds how far you drifted. It's meant to train internal pulse instead of leaning on the click. Does it seem worthwhile?

I'm a tailor, and my book is about trousers. "Hem" follows one pair of corduroys across three brothers. Each page the hem is let down an inch, and the pockets hold what the last boy left: a pebble, a bus ticket, a dried worm. On the final page the youngest hears the jingle and realizes he's wearing his brothers' whole childhoods. Tell me what you think!

I'm a hobby glassblower, and our studio is adding a tiny coffee window. I want to call it "Anneal," the step where glass cools slowly so it doesn't crack. The menu's tagline would be "Slow down. Don't shatter." Thoughts on it?

units:
I'm a dad who started making wooden toys on weekends. Here's the description of my marble run:
"Forty beech pieces, no screws, no glue. Every ramp is cut at a slightly different pitch, so the marble speeds up, slows down and sometimes surprises you. Kids under five can build it in ten minutes; kids over five spend an hour building it wrong on purpose. Sanded smooth, finished in food-safe oil."
What do you think?

Just finished this chorus and I'm kind of buzzing, so I'm sharing it right away. I'm a senior in high school, and it's about my town. Tell me what you think!
Everybody here knows my middle name and my mother's,
the truck my dad sold, the fence I drove through.
I'm leaving in June with one bag and no one's blessing.
God, I hope someplace else knows me half as well as you.

My grandmother takes seven pills a day and gets confused about which she's had. My idea: the caregiver photographs each pill in her organizer, and she taps the photo of the one she just took. No reading required. The family gets one quiet summary each evening, not constant alerts. I'd like to know what you think before I show it to my aunts.

Bootcamp student here. I needed to turn nested config into flat keys and ended up with this recursive version. How would you rate it?
```js
const flat = (o, p = '') =>
  Object.entries(o).flatMap(([k, v]) =>
    v && typeof v === 'object' ? flat(v, p + k + '.') : [[p + k, v]]);
Object.fromEntries(flat({ a: { b: 1, c: { d: 2 } } }));
```

Here's my logline. I'm a long-haul trucker, 50, and I write in the cab at rest stops: "With six hours to his deadline, a trucker picks up a hitchhiker who can tell him exactly how many miles he has left to live, and it's fewer than the distance to his daughter's wedding." Thoughts?

I'm a grad student and my band needs a chorus for our new single. Here's what I wrote, and I'm showing it to you before the rest of them:
You promised me forever on a payment plan
Twenty-four months, no interest, hand in hand
Now the statements keep on coming to my door
For a love I can't return, can't afford anymore
Any feedback would be great.

Our neighborhood association wants to cut down the old oak beside the church to add 14 parking spots. I'm speaking against it: "That oak is 140 years old. Parking lots get repaved every twenty years; trees can only be cut once. You can always add spaces later. You can't add a hundred and forty years." I'm 71 and not much of a public speaker. Is it enough?

I'm 12 and this is my opening for our debate club. The motion is that homework should be abolished. Can you give me feedback? "My opponent says homework builds discipline. Fine. If discipline is the goal, let's assign something honest: wash a dish, call a grandparent, wait in a queue without a phone. Those have never once been marked down for neatness."

I'm a weekend woodworker. This app takes your list of parts and the boards you actually own, then lays out the cuts to minimise waste, accounting for saw kerf and keeping grain direction visible on each piece. You'd get a printable diagram for each board. I'd love an honest reaction, since I mostly just use it on my own projects.

I'm putting this on my dog-grooming flyer: "Your dog can't tell you his ears hurt. He can only shake his head and look at you. A groomer sees mats, ticks, and lumps weeks before a vet appointment would. Book every six weeks and you get a clean dog and a second set of eyes." Does the tone feel right to you?

units: I'm opening a cafe that serves coffee by day and natural wine by night. I'd name it "Zenith & Nadir," the highest and lowest points, one for each half of the day. I'd value hearing what you think of it.

I taught fourth grade for 34 years and I'm applying to be a docent at the natural history museum. This is my paragraph: "Every September I handed my students a whale vertebra I'd bought at a yard sale and said nothing for a full minute. The questions they asked in that silence taught me more about teaching than any training did. I'd like to bring that minute of silence to your visitors." Could you tell me what you make of it?

Hi! I'm a sophomore and I've been writing haiku between study sessions. Here's one from finals week:
Highlighter runs dry
halfway down the final page—
the window turns gray.
Any feedback would be appreciated.

Hobbyist trying some fine-dining tricks at home. Tomato water: blend 2kg ripe tomatoes with 15g salt, basil stems and a splash of sherry vinegar, then hang in cheesecloth overnight without squeezing. Set 500ml of the clear liquid with 3 gelatin sheets, and serve cold over burrata and charred corn with basil oil. I'm a bit nervous to share this. Any advice?

I've kept bees for six winters and finally tried to capture the sound in a haiku:
January hive—
I press my ear to the wood
and hear them, still there
What's your take? I'm especially unsure how the last line is read by someone outside beekeeping.

Drama club president here! We need $2,500 to stage Our Town. My opening: "We will perform a play with no scenery in a gym with too much of it: banners, bleachers, a scoreboard stuck at 42–38. Our Town asks the audience to imagine everything. We only need lights, a rented ladder, and you." Tell me what you think?

I'm 16 and I made a plan for our tiny 1.5m x 3m balcony to help pollinators. West-facing, so hot. Back rail: lavender in long troughs. Middle tier: a 3-step shelf with creeping thyme, borage and calendula. Floor: a shallow saucer of pebbles and water for bees. Hanging baskets along the front with nasturtiums, trailing down so there's something flowering from April to October. Do you have any thoughts?

I'm an undergrad writing my history honours thesis. My question is: "Why did Ottoman port authorities in Salonica begin recording ship cargoes in French in the 1880s, and what does that choice reveal about who the records were meant for?" What's your opinion?

I run a weekend food truck and this is my birria. Short rib and goat shoulder, 2:1. Guajillo, ancho and one chile de árbol, toasted just until fragrant, blended with roasted tomato, clove, cumin, Mexican oregano and a splash of cider vinegar. Braise 3.5 hours at 160°C. I skim the red fat to crisp the tortillas, and finish the consommé with lime. What would you change, if anything?

units: I've been a newspaper copy editor for thirty years and I'm trying screenwriting. Logline: "Two obituary writers at a dying small-town paper, long at war over each other's prose, each begin secretly writing the other's obituary, the most honest work either has done in years." What do you make of it?

Casual question: I'm 45, sit at a desk nine hours a day, and my shoulders are creeping forward. Mon/Thu: rows, face pulls, wall angels, dead bugs. Tue/Fri: hip flexor stretch, glute bridges, goblet squats, 20-minute walk. Wed: swim or bike, whatever. Weekend: one hike. Plus a 2-minute doorway chest stretch every time my coffee finishes. Does this make sense? Roast me if needed.

I'm three weeks into a new job and my manager asked for onboarding feedback. Here's my reply. Does it seem fair and useful?
"Hi Danielle, what's working: shadowing Kofi. What slowed me: I waited six days for system access. I've drafted a day-one checklist (attached) from what I wish I'd had. Happy to be the guinea pig for the next hire."

I taught high school English for 34 years and now I'm learning dessert. Lemon posset: simmer 2 cups heavy cream with ¾ cup sugar for 3 minutes, then whisk in ⅓ cup lemon juice and 1 tbsp olive oil. Pour into glasses and chill for 4 hours. Serve with rosemary shortbread. The olive oil makes it taste silky and slightly grassy. Would you like to tell me what you think?

I'm a hobby woodworker, and I'm turning my workshop into a Saturday-morning cafe. The name I've chosen is "Dovetail," for the joint that holds because of how the pieces fit together, like neighbors. What's your take on it?

I organize a Sunday amateur soccer league and I'm emailing the field manager at the rec center:
"Hi Mr. Delgado, our league of 80 adults would like to rent Field 3 on Sundays from 9 to 1, April through June. We'll bring our own cones, lock the gate after, and pay $400 upfront. We also pick up trash after each game, and our referees are certified. Could we meet Thursday to confirm dates? Best, Farid"
What do you think?

I'm a high school junior and wrote this for a film club pitch night. "When a stroke leaves her grandfather speaking only the Cantonese he spent fifty years hiding, a sixteen-year-old who never learned it has one summer to decode his confession." How would you react to this as a pitch?

I'm a copy editor, and my cafe is called "Em Dash." The tagline on the window will read: "A pause worth taking." I wanted the name to be small and typographic and to say something about slowing down mid-sentence. I've stared at it for so long that I can't judge it anymore. Could you tell me what you think?

Proud to finally share this. I'm a Mumbai-based sound editor, 52, and it's the first story I've written myself: "In 1950s Bombay, the unseen playback singer behind a film star's voice must decide whether to expose her when the star's husband falls in love with the voice and not the woman." How does it strike you?

I'm a medical historian drafting a lecture. My thesis: "Semmelweis's handwashing data was rejected not because physicians were stupid but because it implied that physicians themselves were killing their patients; evidence is accepted most slowly when it indicts the self-image of the people asked to believe it." What do you think?

units:
I run a small blog about hiking and wrote this to make URL slugs. Would you mind telling me what you think?
```python
import re, unicodedata
def slugify(title):
    ascii_ = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", ascii_.lower()).strip("-")
```

I'm a new dad (38) and I wrote this lullaby chorus at 3 a.m. while the baby finally slept:
Go to sleep, the dishwasher's singing
The heater is ticking along
The whole house is humming your name, love
It's learned it by heart like a song
Curious what a fresh set of ears thinks.

Just a casual one: I teach myself screenwriting on YouTube and wrote this logline. "In 1889, a widowed schoolteacher enters the Oklahoma Land Run on a borrowed mule, carrying her husband's ashes and a map she has just realized he forged." Thoughts? Anything you'd change?

I'm a 20-year-old intern and somehow I was asked to speak for our founder. I said: 'I've known Mr. Reyes for eleven weeks. In that time he learned my name, my coffee order, and the name of my cat. I'm told he also started a company. I'll take people's word for it. But anyone who remembers the intern's cat has already built something that lasts.' Was that too bold?

I'm a 26-year-old teacher in Leeds. Take-home £2,100: rent £780; council tax £95; bills £110; groceries £230; train £70; phone £18; Lifetime ISA £250 (for the 25% bonus); student loan overpay £120; fun £150; gifts £40; holiday pot £137; buffer £100. I'd love to know what you think, honestly.

I'm a grad student who writes songs to cope with deadlines. This chorus is about my grandfather's radio, which I still keep on my desk. Does it work as a chorus, in your view?
He tuned it by feel, a quarter inch of static,
found the ballgame in the hiss like a man finding a door.
Now it sits on my desk, picking up nothing,
but I turn the dial anyway. I just want to hear it once more.

I'm a college junior and I've been writing a coming-of-age novel about a boxing gym. Here's the first line: "The summer I turned sixteen I learned two things about my father's gym: that it smelled of liniment and forgiveness, and that nobody ever came there to win." Could you give me feedback?

Retired baker, still experimenting. Rye and caraway sourdough discard crackers: 150g discard, 60g rye flour, 40g olive oil, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp caraway seeds. Mix, rest 30 minutes, roll paper thin, brush with water, and sprinkle with flaky salt and more seeds. Bake at 180°C for 18 minutes, rotating once, until they're deep amber and snap. I'd like a second opinion, please.

Six months post ACL reconstruction. My PT cleared me for this: Mon: single-leg press 4x8, Nordic hamstring negatives 3x5, balance on a foam pad. Tue: stationary bike 30 min. Wed: step-downs, hip bridges, calf raises. Thu: rest. Fri: light jogging intervals, 1 min on/2 min walk x8. Sat: swim. Sun: rest. I track knee swelling after each session. I'd appreciate your thoughts, I'm kind of anxious about it.

units:
I own a little flower shop and scribble haiku on receipt paper after weddings. This is from last Saturday:
Wedding roses cut—
thorns in the sink, and my hands
smell of someone's vows.
What do you make of it?

I'm 16 and I designed a logo for our robotics team, the Gearheads. It's a gear with 44 teeth, our team number, but one tooth is missing. The gap is shaped exactly like the jaw of an open-end wrench, so it looks like the tool is meant to slot in and finish the gear. Orange on black. Any feedback would be awesome, thanks!

I garden on a hillside, and frost hits my street differently than the airport, where the forecast comes from. My idea is Cold Pocket. Neighbors within 1 km submit their overnight lows with one tap. After a few weeks, the app learns that my lower terrace runs 3°C colder. Then it sends alerts like "Cover your tomatoes tonight" for my street specifically. Would you try something like this?

I'm trying out new material at an open mic next week and I'm a bit nervous. The bit: "My ex was a cartographer. He said I was distorted at the edges. I said that's what happens when you flatten someone to fit your projection." Could you tell me how it reads?

Nurse of 11 years trying to move into UX research. Here's my pitch paragraph, please be straight with me: "I have run roughly 40,000 usability tests, though we called them shifts. I know exactly where your charting software fails: 3 a.m., one hand gloved, during a rapid response. I can't yet build a Figma prototype as polished as yours, but I can tell you which button a frightened person will press first." What do you think?

I've been an owner-operator trucker for 14 years. Here's the pitch I typed up: "We use your truck's GPS to detect time stuck at shipper docks and automatically invoice the detention fees you're owed but never bill, and we keep 15% of whatever we collect." Honestly curious what an outsider thinks.

I'm a planetary scientist and I wrote a comic sci-fi novel for fun. The opening line: "Technically, I am the last human on Mars, but the robots have been very nice about it." My friends laughed, but they're my friends. What's your opinion?

I'm a college sophomore and baked these for my floor. Brown butter miso cookies: brown 170g butter, chill until solid. Cream with 100g dark brown sugar, 50g white sugar, 1 tbsp white miso. Add 1 egg plus 1 yolk, 1 tsp vanilla, 220g flour, ½ tsp baking soda, ½ tsp salt. Fold in 150g chopped 70% chocolate. Rest dough 36 hours, bake at 180°C for 11 minutes, flaky salt on top. Honest thoughts on the recipe?

I work closing shifts at a cinema and made a suggestion to my manager. Here's the email:
"Hi Paula, closing takes us 55 minutes because we sweep each theater after cleaning the concession counter. If one person starts on the theaters while the other counts the till, I timed it at 35 minutes in a trial last Friday. It means everyone leaves earlier and the floors get cleaned while the popcorn is still warm. Can I show you the checklist? Thanks, Devon"
What do you think?

Call centre agent, 22. I wrote this to my team leader about something I built. How does it look?
"Hi Yusuf, 30% of my calls this week were 'where's my refund?' I wrote a reply template that states the five-day timeline in the first sentence and links tracking. My repeat contacts dropped from 11 to 4. Can I share it with the team on Thursday?"

Hi! For my databases course I had to list every consecutive-day login streak per user. Here's my Postgres attempt:
WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_at::date AS d FROM logins),
g AS (SELECT user_id, d, d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY d))::int AS grp FROM d)

I'm a sysadmin and I've been burned by half-written config files, so I made this:
```python
def atomic_write(path, data):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
            f.write(data)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        os.unlink(tmp)
        raise
```
What's your opinion?

units: Hello, I'm a brewer starting Low Tide Brewing. The logo is a pint glass in outline. The foam line at the top is a flat horizon, and below it, the beer is filled with faint sand ripples, the pattern left on a beach when the water goes out. One line weight throughout, cream on navy. I'd really like your take on it.

Hi! For my nursing capstone I came up with this: "Among night-shift nurses on medical-surgical wards, does a protected 20-minute nap during breaks reduce medication administration errors in the final three hours of shift compared with caffeine alone?" I'm a bit nervous about showing my advisor. Thoughts?

I run a coffee cart near the train station. This one's about a regular. Any thoughts would be great:
The first customer is always the widower.
He orders two cups
and drinks the one that's his
slowly,
so the other can stay warm.

Accountant, 38, trying to switch into film production accounting. How's this paragraph? "I've audited a hospital, a shipping company, and a minor-league baseball team, and the most honest ledger belonged to the baseball team's snack stand. I like small chaos with receipts. Give me forty crew, cash per diems, and a location that changes on Thursday, and I'll hand you books that balance by Friday."

I'm a first-generation college grad, writing the opening for our alumni scholarship fund. "Dear fellow alumni, I was the first person in my family to open a college acceptance letter, and my mother made me read it aloud three times to be sure. The fourth time she asked how much. This letter is about the fourth time." I'd love your feedback.

I'm a chef and I've been asked to speak at a food conference, which feels odd because I usually just cook. My opening: "Salt is the only rock we eat on purpose, and for ten thousand years we've argued about which ones taste best." What do you think?

Pareto analysis for our catalogue: what share of revenue the top products make. I added the tie-breaker and ROWS frame deliberately.
WITH r AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(revenue) AS rev FROM sales GROUP BY product_id)
SELECT product_id, rev,
  SUM(rev) OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) / SUM(rev) OVER () AS cum_share
FROM r ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id;
I'm a finance manager, not a developer. Does this look right to you?

I'm a 1600-rated club chess player writing up a project for fun. My question: "For players rated 1400 to 1800 in 15+10 online games, do time-trouble blunders cost more rating points than opening errors, and does that balance shift after a player's first thirty games?" I'd use Lichess data. Would love any opinion you have!

I'm a grad student, writing a short story about my grandmother. Sharing the first paragraph with some nerves: "The telegram came on a Tuesday, which my grandmother held against Tuesdays for the rest of her life. She forgave the postman, the war, and eventually God. But Tuesdays she kept, the way a dog keeps a bone, and so for sixty years, every week, we ate cold supper and did not answer the door." What do you think?

```python
def needs_water(rain_mm, threshold=15, decay=0.7):
```

units:
I run a food truck downtown and write haiku on my lunch break. Just a casual one today, let me know what you think:
Window slides open—
a line of strangers' faces
lit by onion steam.

I'm a taxi driver, 40, and I moved here eleven years ago. I've been turning my feelings into songs. This is the chorus of the newest:
I wear two watches, one for here, one for home
One says it's noon, one says you're asleep
I live in the hours that don't have a name
Keeping time for the ones I can't keep
I'd be grateful for your opinion.

Art history student. I tried to make my bio sound like a museum placard. Does it come across? Tell me what you think.
"Subject: 24-year-old, oil on tired. Origin: Ohio, relocated for the sake of a thesis on Dutch still lifes. Notable features: a laugh louder than the room requires, an unreasonable tote bag collection. On view weekends only. Seeking a viewer who'll linger, ask good questions, and doesn't whisper in galleries unless it's gossip."

Philosophy grad student here. Here's my thesis for a seminar paper: "The trolley problem endures not because it reveals our moral intuitions but because it strips away the substance of moral life, relationships of prior obligation, so its answers describe only how people behave toward strangers they will never meet." Where would you push on it?

I'm 65 and just retired after 40 years as a high school band director. At my party I said: 'Forty years of teenagers, and I've heard every wrong note a human can play. I miss none of them. I miss all of them. Please don't clap on one and three. And if you must cry, do it in tempo.' Casually curious how that works on paper.

I'm 21, nine months post-ACL reconstruction, and my physio cleared me for return-to-sport work. Mon: single-leg press 4x8 with a 3-second lower, Nordics 3x5. Tue: low box jumps with stuck landings 4x5, deceleration drills. Thu: heavy RDLs, hip thrusts. Fri: straight-line runs 6x60 m at 80%. Sat: pool. Wed/Sun: off. Hop tests are next month, so I'm tracking limb symmetry. Feedback?

I'm 16 and I'd like to redo Eratosthenes. I teamed up with a student at a school 410 km due north of mine through an online club. On the same day at local solar noon, we each measure a vertical stick's shadow and compute the sun angle, then use the angle difference and the distance to estimate Earth's circumference. I'll also propagate the measurement uncertainty to see whether we can tell our answer apart from 40,075 km. Thoughts?

I'm a literary translator replying to a post claiming AI will make us obsolete: "Translation isn't swapping words. It's deciding what to lose. Every sentence of Chekhov costs something in English, and someone has to choose the price. A machine can hand you the menu. It can't tell you which dish to give up, or sit with you while you grieve it." Posting this tonight. Would you share it?

I'm a self-taught programmer applying for a junior developer role at a logistics company. This is the paragraph where I talk about my project. Can you tell me what you think?
"My grandmother runs a four-person courier service and tracked deliveries in a spiral notebook. I built her a small app that texts customers when a driver is ten minutes away. Missed handoffs fell by a third. She still keeps the notebook, though, and I learned that good software has to coexist with it."

Language-learning student here, wrote this for my Instagram: "Day 100 of Korean. I can order coffee, apologize to a bus driver, and read every sign on my street. I still can't understand my girlfriend's grandmother, who speaks in dialect and laughter. Day 101 goal: the laughter." Any feedback?

units: Hi! I play chess competitively as a hobby, and I'm toasting two fellow club members. Here goes: "In chess, we say the opening is theory, the middlegame is imagination, and the endgame is technique. Raj and Claire skipped the opening, played a wildly imaginative middlegame in the club parking lot, and now they're in an endgame where the only rule is that nobody resigns. May every draw be by agreement. To Raj and Claire." Thoughts?

I'm a vegan and only a year into cooking. These are king oyster "scallops": cut stems into 2 cm thick rounds, score the tops in a crosshatch, and sear in a dry cast iron pan with a weight on top until deep brown. Then add olive oil and white miso whisked with lemon, and baste for 1 minute. Serve on pea purée with chive oil. How does it sound to you?

I run a tiny karaoke bar in Manila and I've been turning my regulars into a script. Logline: "Every Thursday for eleven years, a stranger has sung the same ballad at a karaoke bar; when he stops coming, the tone-deaf owner learns the song and sets out to find him." Thoughts?

I'm 22, bilingual, and I wrote this chorus about my mom making tortillas before work:
Mi mamá cuenta el mundo en tortillas
One for the rent, one for the rain
Dos para mí, y una para la esperanza
Flip it quick before it burns again
I'd really like to know what you think, especially about mixing the languages.

I'm a retired cabinetmaker, 68, and my daughter talked me into a dating site. Here's the bio: "I can tell what's wrong with your drawers by the sound they make. Widowed three years, ready for company that argues about whether the crossword is cheating if you look up one answer. I make soup on Sundays, always too much. Bring a bowl and an opinion on dovetails." What do you make of it?

I'm 80 and my granddaughter said I should show someone. It's a story from my childhood, dressed up a bit:
"The summer I was nine, the circus came to Ballina and left without its elephant. Nobody could explain it. She stood in Mr. Doyle's field for six weeks, enormous and patient, eating his hay, until the whole parish had told her something it had never told another living soul."
What do you think, dear?

Pascal's triangle as an infinite generator. I just love how the zip trick works out, and I'm a 52-year-old accountant who picked up Python during lockdown:
```python
def pascal():
    row = [1]
    while True:
        yield row
        row = [a + b for a, b in zip([0] + row, row + [0])]
```
What do you make of it?

I'm 81 and this is the first poem I've ever shown anyone. My granddaughter set up this chat for me. I'd be glad to hear what you think.
At eighty I price the stairs by breath:
the fourth one costs a nickel,
the ninth, a dime.
I reach the landing, solvent still,
and spend what's left on the window.

I'm in an MFA program and workshopping this next week. Before I do, I'd like a fresh reader's take, especially on the line breaks:
The heron holds the river's one idea
so still the water starts to doubt itself.
Then the small bright argument
of a minnow, and the whole grey sentence
resolves into a throat.

I'm a plumber and I came up with this for the side of my van: "Every house has one pipe that's been quietly holding a grudge since 1974." My wife says it's too long for a van. Be straight with me: would you read it, and would you call me?

units: I'm a night-shift nurse in Phoenix, and I designed a garden I can enjoy at dusk with no lawn. The layout: a decomposed granite courtyard, a central ring of boulders around a palo verde for shade, agave and red yucca on the south edge, and a night-blooming cereus and white evening primrose along the patio. A drip line runs on one timer, three zones. Total water use is under 15% of our old lawn. What's your take?

After 30 years as a newspaper reporter, I'm opening a cafe in the old Gazette building, and I'm calling it "Stop Press." The menu will be printed on broadsheet and the coffee will be strong enough to meet a deadline. Does the name have the right ring to it? Tell me straight, I've had worse feedback from editors.

I make a small podcast about local history from my closet, and I'm applying for a radio producer job. Here's the paragraph on my work. Can you tell me what you think?
"Episode 14 is eleven minutes about the 1952 flood, and nine of them are one woman, Dolores, describing the sound of the river at night. I cut my own questions to almost nothing. A producer's job, I've learned, is to build a quiet room and then leave it."

Long-time fantasy reader, first-time writer here. My novel begins: "Tuesday was the day Thornwick hid its children, so the dragon's tax collector found only goats, a very old man, and an unusually loud silence." Would you tell me what you think? Be gentle, I'm a bit anxious about this.

I'm applying for a historical marker for the old Delmar Bakery on 5th Street. Our statement opens: "For 41 years this building fed the neighborhood on credit. A ledger still hangs on the back wall, recording striking miners' debts the owner never collected. Towns are remembered for their monuments, but they're held together by their bakeries." How does it read to you?

I've dispatched for a regional trucking company for eight years and want to move into logistics analysis. Here's my bullet: "Rerouted a 40-truck fleet using a weather- and traffic-weighted spreadsheet model I built, cutting deadhead miles 17% and saving about 31,000 gallons of diesel per year." Mind giving me your opinion?

Proposal to my team to kill our "smart suggestions" feature. Key paragraph: "Suggestions are used by 3% of users and generate 31% of our support tickets. Every feature is a promise to maintain it forever. We aren't deleting a feature; we're refusing a lifelong loan with a 3% return. Cut it, and move those two engineers to search, which 90% of users touch daily." Sending it Monday. Any thoughts first?

I'm an occupational therapist, and this is my layout for a sensory garden in a dementia care home. A looped path, 1.5m wide, with no dead ends, so no one gets stuck. Along it, five stations: scent (lavender, rosemary), touch (lamb's ear, grasses), sound (bamboo, wind chimes), taste (raspberries, mint) and a familiar-memory corner with a washing line and a shed. Handrails run along the edges, and the seating is every 12m. Would you give me your thoughts?

I'm a 24-year-old ballet dancer, rehearsing six days a week, so cross-training can't add leg fatigue. Mon: 10 minutes of pre-class glute band work. Tue: Pilates reformer. Wed: upper body only, push-ups and rows, 3x10. Thu: slow single-leg calf raises 3x15, tibialis raises. Fri: nothing. Sat: 20 minutes of easy bike. Sun: complete rest, no stretching. Would you change anything?

I'm 40 and a T10 paraplegic. I want to build strength without wrecking my shoulders. Mon: seated cable rows 4x10, face pulls 3x15, landmine press 3x8. Tue: handcycle intervals, 6x2 min hard/2 easy. Wed: rest. Thu: lat pulldowns 4x8, parallel-bar dips 3x6, rotator cuff band work. Fri: 30-minute steady handcycle. Sat: Pallof presses and core. Sun: rest. Pulling volume is double pushing on purpose. Thoughts?

units:
I do auto repair for a living and write poems on the side, which my staff find hilarious. Here's one:
Customer says it makes a noise
but only when she isn't there.
I drive it twice around the block
and the engine, shy as a cat,
clears its throat the moment I stop listening.
What do you think?

I'm a baker who codes on the side, and this turns recipe timings like "1h 30m" into milliseconds for my proofing timer. Thoughts?
```js
const units = { d: 864e5, h: 36e5, m: 6e4, s: 1e3 };
const toMs = str =>
  [...str.matchAll(/(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([dhms])/g)]
    .reduce((t, [, n, u]) => t + n * units[u], 0);
```

I'm an architect and wrote this on LinkedIn about a library we just finished: "Every building is an argument. This library says: sit down, nobody's selling you anything. That's why the windows are low. We designed them so a child could watch the rain from a beanbag." My colleagues said it was fine, but they're my friends. What do you honestly think?

I'm a barista and I write haiku on receipt paper during slow shifts, lol. Here's one from today:
Rush over. The foam
heart I made begins to blur
toward the cup's edge
what do u think?

I'm an undergrad raising $3,000 to sequence soil from my grandmother's farm. Here's my opening, and I'm a bit anxious about it: "My grandmother says the south field is tired. I study microbes, so I asked what tired means. A teaspoon of that soil holds billions of organisms, and I'd like to find out which ones have quit." How does it land for you?

I'm a volunteer firefighter and this is my pitch for a side business: "We sell rural fire departments a $4,000-a-year subscription that replaces paper pre-incident plans with drone-mapped 3D layouts of every farm, so crews know where the anhydrous ammonia tank and the old propane shed are before the truck arrives." Be honest, what's your take?

I spent twelve years as a paralegal and I'm opening a cafe across from the county courthouse. The name: "Grounds for Appeal." Lawyers and jurors will be my main customers. Does it work for you, or would you change anything?

Apprentice electrician, just finished my hours and building my first resume. Here's what I wrote: "Completed 8,000 apprenticeship hours with zero recordable safety incidents; independently ran conduit and terminated a 400A service for a 24-unit apartment retrofit, passing inspection on the first visit." What do you think?

I'm a Dungeon Master and posted this on r/DnD: "My players found a door that only opened if you told it the truth. Three hours later the paladin admitted he'd never liked his god, and the door was still locked. It was waiting for the rogue." Does it land for you?

I'm a linguistics major, and my idea is menu rewrites for immigrant-owned restaurants. Not translation, but descriptions that explain a dish to local diners: 'Injera: a spongy sourdough flatbread you eat with your hands. Yes, it's meant to be shared.' $90 flat, with a printed table card. I did two for free near campus and both owners said customers started asking for the dishes by name. Could this be a real business?

units: I volunteer in a hospice kitchen. Our residents often want something gentle, so I made this ginger chicken congee. Simmer 1 cup jasmine rice in 8 cups chicken stock with 5 thick slices of ginger and a bone-in thigh for 90 minutes. Shred the chicken and stir it back in. Top with scallion, a drizzle of toasted sesame oil, and a little white pepper. Honest opinion welcome.

I run a small lawn-care company and I'm applying for a small-business loan, so I'm rewriting my bio into resume form. Here's the main bullet: "Grew a one-truck lawn-care business to $186K annual revenue in three years; converted 70% of customers to seasonal contracts by texting before-and-after photos after every visit." What's your reaction?

Posted this in our neighbourhood Facebook group this morning and now I'm second-guessing it: "To whoever left a bag of lemons on the bus shelter bench with a note saying 'free, too many': I drove the 14 for thirty-one years and nobody ever left anything for strangers. I took one. It's in my tea. Thank you." Is it okay, or too sappy? I'm 67 and new to this.

I'm 16 and I designed a logo for our robotics team, the Gearheads. It's a gear with 44 teeth, our team number, but one tooth is missing. The gap is shaped exactly like the jaw of an open-end wrench, so it looks like the tool is meant to slot in and finish the gear. Orange on black. Any feedback would be awesome, thanks!

I'm 80 and my granddaughter said I should show someone. It's a story from my childhood, dressed up a bit:
"The summer I was nine, the circus came to Ballina and left without its elephant. Nobody could explain it. She stood in Mr. Doyle's field for six weeks, enormous and patient, eating his hay, until the whole parish had told her something it had never told another living soul."
What do you think, dear?

I drive long-haul and write on the notes app at truck stops. This one came to me in Nebraska. What's your take?
Nebraska takes an hour to finish a sentence.
The grain elevators raise their one white word
and drop it behind me.
Somewhere past Kearney I say your name
to the windshield, which holds it a mile and lets go.

I'm 72 and I've sewn for fifty years. My idea is adaptive clothing alterations. I'd convert people's own favorite shirts and trousers with magnetic buttons, side-opening seams and soft tags, for people with arthritis or limited mobility. My slogan is: "Keep the shirt you love. Change how it opens." I charge $18 per garment. I'm a little shy about putting this out there. Please tell me what you think.

I'm Nigerian, studying in Leeds, and this is my party jollof. Blend roasted red peppers, tomatoes, scotch bonnet and onion, then fry the base in oil for about 25 minutes until it separates. Add thyme, curry powder, bay and stock. Parboiled rice, sealed with foil under the lid, finishing on low so the bottom catches lightly. Butter at the end. How does the method read to you?

I'm a finish carpenter applying for a set builder job at a theater. Wrote this: "Furniture is built to last fifty years. A set is built to look like it will, for six weeks, and then be burned. I find that freeing. I can fake a hundred-year-old oak door from luan and one can of walnut stain, and I can make it survive a slammed exit every night." Does that work, do you think?

units: Just a casual share from a night-shift security guard who writes screenplays on his breaks: "Three octogenarian sisters plan to steal their late father's violin back from the museum that bought it from a forger, but the only one who can authenticate it is the sister who hasn't spoken to them in thirty years." Opinions?
My coffee cart outside the train station needs a chalkboard line. I wrote: "Dark roast, bright side." Would you say it fits a morning commuter crowd? Let me know what you think!

I'm a chess club coach opening a quick takeaway cafe next to the park tables where people play. I'd like to name it "En Passant," the chess capture made in passing. Is the name clear and appealing to you? Be candid.

I'm 71 and I knit blankets to sell at the craft fair. My granddaughter told me to ask people online for opinions. This is my tag:
"Merino cot blanket, knitted in honeycomb stitch, which holds warmth without weight. Washed in lanolin so it stays soft. Nine evenings of work. Machine washable on the wool cycle, and made to be handed down: the edges are bound twice, because babies are hard on everything."
Does it work?

I'm a retired electrician and this is my first poem since school. I wrote it about my mother's house:
I rewired my mother's house in 1987.
Behind the plaster, still, her wedding year:
cloth-wrapped cable, brittle as old licorice,
still carrying, without complaint,
the little the house had asked of it.
What would you say to it, honestly?

I'm a development associate at a food bank applying for a director role. This is the bullet I'm sharing in my cover letter too: "Secured $480K in first-time foundation grants by pitching 23 funders; raised donor retention from 38% to 54% by personally calling every donor who gave over $100." How does it land for you?

I'm 38, newly divorced, and my sister made me write one of these. Here's what I came up with. What's your reaction?
"Recently learned to cook for one without making enough for four. Looking for someone to help me fail at that. I own too many cast iron pans, one very old cat, and a strong opinion about rice. Funny in person, quieter in text. Come find out which."

I own a small bakery and I'm writing a post to explain our prices. Title: "Why Our Croissants Cost $4.50." First sentence: "A croissant is three days of waiting disguised as breakfast: one day for the dough, one for the butter to settle into it, and one for me to stop touching it." Could you tell me your impressions?

Our knitting group has two speeds: "I'll finish it by Christmas" and "Which Christmas?" I said that at last week's meetup and got a laugh, but I'm wondering whether it holds up written down. What do you think, any tweaks?

I do alterations and slow-fashion tailoring, and I'm designing my logo. A yellow measuring tape curls into a spiral like a snail shell, its numbers getting smaller toward the middle. A small snail head and two feelers come out at the outer end. 'Slow Stitch' is stitched in dashes beneath it. I'm curious what you think.

units: Here's the opening line of my historical novel, set in 1880s Hungary: "The year the river changed its mind, my father sold our cow, our name, and nearly me." I'm a history student and I've been staring at this one for ages. Any feedback would be welcome.

I'm a club chess player, 52, and I blog about my games. This one's titled "I Lost to an Eight-Year-Old and Here's the Move That Did It." It begins: "She pushed her h-pawn on move six, I laughed, and for the next forty minutes I learned that being amused is the most expensive mistake in chess." Honest feedback welcome!

We run a small vegetable farm with a CSA of 60 members. My idea: members can swap items in their box until Wednesday night, like trading kale for extra carrots. The app then sends us a harvest list adjusted by swaps, so we pick what's wanted. It also shows a 'surplus' list for cheap add-ons. Could you tell me what you think?

I'm opening a chess café named En Passant. The logo is a pawn in solid black, front-on. But its round head is a coffee cup seen from above: a ring, dark liquid inside, and a small handle at the right side where a pawn would have nothing. Everything else is perfectly standard. I'd like your opinion, please.

Film studies sophomore, and I'm excited about this paper. Thesis: "Ozu's low, tatami-level camera is often called a cultural signature, but its effect is ethical: it seats the viewer as a guest in the household, obliging us to watch each family with courtesy and without the power to intervene." What's your opinion?

I farm a few acres and write stories in the winter. Here's the beginning of one, if you'd give me your honest reaction: "Ma used to say the wind in Dry Fork had opinions. The morning it started whispering our names one by one, I figured it had finally made up its mind about us. Pa ignored it. Pa had ignored most things, including the well, which had been dry since March and had the manners to be quiet about it."

I'm a vet tech and my colleagues keep telling me to write down the stuff I say. This one came up on Tuesday: "Every vet knows the animal is rarely the one who needs sedating." I'd love to hear what someone outside the clinic thinks.

I'm a nursing student, and I was asked to say a few words for Carol, a night-shift nurse retiring after 38 years: "Carol taught me that 3 a.m. is when patients tell the truth. Hold the hand, she said, lower the lights, and wait. Thirty-eight years of waiting with strangers so they weren't alone. I may never be as good, but I'll be awake, and that was the first thing she taught me." Honest opinion?

I'm cataloguing my vinyl collection in Postgres with a tags array. Wanted live jazz albums but no Christmas ones:
CREATE INDEX albums_tags_gin ON albums USING gin (tags);
SELECT title, artist
FROM albums
WHERE tags @> ARRAY['jazz', 'live']
  AND NOT tags && ARRAY['christmas']
ORDER BY artist, title;
I'd love to know how this strikes you.

Music theory student here, and I'm opening my class presentation at the piano: "Play any two notes a half-step apart and you'll feel uneasy. That unease is why the shark in Jaws works, and I'm going to show you how to make it with two fingers." Would love to hear what you think.

units: Our daughter cried when the snow melted, so I wrote this on my lunch breaks. "Snowman, Stored." Odile hides her snowman in the chest freezer between the peas and Dad's fish, visiting daily with a scarf. By July he's the size of a grapefruit. In December she introduces him to the first snowfall like a returning relative. I'm a plumber, not an author. Thoughts?

I own a small brewery and want a beer garden that supports what we brew. Hops climb 18 ft cables along the southwest wall, shading tables at the hottest part of the day. Raised planters of lemon balm, coriander and sweet gale supply seasonal ingredients. Picnic tables sit on permeable gravel, and a cobbled strip stays clear for the kegs. Chalk labels on each plant let people taste the connection. Any feedback?

My used bookshop is called The Dog-Eared Page. For the logo, I imagined a simple page in cream, with its top corner folded down. The fold is shaped as a floppy dog ear, with one small ink dot for an eye on the folded part. Everything else is blank paper. Thoughts? Be as blunt as you like.

Flattening JSON order items in Postgres. Our orders come from three vendors, so the key isn't always present:
SELECT o.id, item->>'sku' AS sku, (item->>'qty')::int AS qty
FROM orders o
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(o.payload->'items') AS item
WHERE o.payload ? 'items';
Backend dev, 2 years of experience. I'd like your thoughts, especially on whether I'm missing something.

Quick one from a 26-year-old barista: "A court stenographer who has silently typed every word of eleven thousand trials is subpoenaed to testify, and discovers she is the only person who remembers what was actually said." What do you think? I'm planning to enter it in a screenwriting fellowship.
For my marketing class I invented an alarm clock that wakes you with gradual sunlight. My slogan is "Sunrise, minus the rooster." Can you give me feedback? My professor wants peer opinions.

I'm a farmer, new to writing. In the town of Marl, your umbrella opens onto whatever you're feeling: Grandpa's makes drizzle, the mayor's makes hail. Nell's opens only sunshine, because she never lets anyone see her sad. The day it finally drizzles over her, the whole town comes to stand underneath. Tell me what you think, please.

I drive the Route 9 bus and write poems on my breaks. This is from the last run of the night. What do you think?
Route 9, final run. The bus exhales.
Rows of seats keep the shapes of strangers,
a dent here, a warmth there,
and I drive the empty ghosts back to the depot
with my headlights on for them.

I'm a 62-year-old dairy farmer. At my neighbor Walt's retirement, I said: 'Walt farmed the same hundred and sixty acres as his father. People call that standing still. But I watched him walk that fence line every morning for forty years, and the ground under him changed more than any of us did. You don't stay in one place by not moving. You stay by tending.' Honest feedback welcome.

I'm a baker, so I'm up at 4am anyway. My cafe opens at 6:30 for the people on early shifts: bus drivers, midwives, cleaners. It's called "Half Past." You'd say, "Meet me at half past," and everybody knows it's an easy hour to get to. Just wondering what comes to mind when you read the name.
