units: Tonight I'm opening our astronomy club's star party. Here's the speech: "The light you'll see in Andromeda left 2.5 million years ago, before anything we'd call human. It has been traveling toward this field, this telescope, this paper cup of cocoa in your hand. Please don't rush. It's waited a long time for you. Red flashlights only, and be kind to the dark." What do you reckon?

Just finished this chorus and I'm kind of buzzing, so I'm sharing it right away. I'm a senior in high school, and it's about my town. Tell me what you think!
Everybody here knows my middle name and my mother's,
the truck my dad sold, the fence I drove through.
I'm leaving in June with one bag and no one's blessing.
God, I hope someplace else knows me half as well as you.

I run a small bakery and I'm mentoring a student with this idea. Sourdough starter in identical clear jars, same flour and hydration, held at 18, 22, 26 and 30°C in water baths. Time-lapse photos mark rise height every 10 minutes. Then we compute peak-rise time and estimate Q10 for fermentation. Three jars per temperature. How would you rate the approach?

I'm a wedding photographer, and this is a pitch email to a couple choosing between me and a cheaper option: "You'll forget the centerpieces and the playlist. In forty years, you'll want your grandmother's hands adjusting your veil, and your father's face a second before he walks you down the aisle. I take only twelve weddings a year, so I can be standing where those moments happen." Should I send it?

Just graduated and applying for backend jobs. This is the first bullet under my internship: "Reduced p95 checkout API latency from 1.8s to 310ms by replacing N+1 Postgres queries with batched lookups and adding a read-through Redis cache, saving an estimated $42K/yr in compute." What do you think? Anything you'd change?

Nursing student here, working on a startup idea for my entrepreneurship elective. The pitch: "Night-shift nurses lose about twenty minutes per shift re-explaining patients at handoff, so we turn a 90-second spoken summary into a structured SBAR note that the incoming nurse approves with one tap." What's your opinion?

Firefighter, 33. Wrote this on shift, be straight with me: "I run toward things for a living, which is why I'm slow to say what I feel. I make a decent chili. I fall asleep during every movie by minute forty. I'll carry your couch up four flights and never mention it. Looking for someone who texts back when I'm off and understands when I can't."

I'm a retired electrician and this is my first poem since school. I wrote it about my mother's house:
I rewired my mother's house in 1987.
Behind the plaster, still, her wedding year:
cloth-wrapped cable, brittle as old licorice,
still carrying, without complaint,
the little the house had asked of it.
What would you say to it, honestly?

For my sociology seminar: "Bureaucratic waiting is usually dismissed as inefficiency, but it functions as power: by treating the citizen's time as cheap and the state's as precious, the DMV queue teaches people their place in the relationship before a single form is stamped." I'd appreciate any feedback on the thesis.

Paralegal here, trying to move into litigation support. I'd love a second pair of eyes on this bullet: "Built a privilege-log template and tagging protocol that cut document review for a 400,000-page antitrust production from an estimated 9 weeks to 5, with zero clawback requests." What's your take?

units: Apprentice electrician, just finished my hours and building my first resume. Here's what I wrote: "Completed 8,000 apprenticeship hours with zero recordable safety incidents; independently ran conduit and terminated a 400A service for a 24-unit apartment retrofit, passing inspection on the first visit." What do you think?

I'm the mayor of a town of 6,000 and I'm campaigning for the library levy. Here's a section of my speech: "A library is the last place in town where you can walk in with no money and nobody asks why you're there. It costs the average household $41 a year. Ask yourself what else you can buy that's open to everyone, including the person you'd never think of." How does that sit with you?

Week 10 of my marathon block, aiming for 3:15. Mon: rest, 15 minutes of yoga. Tue: 8x400 m at 5k pace, 90 s jog. Wed: 10 km easy plus 6 strides. Thu: 16 km with 8 km at marathon pace (4:37/km). Fri: rest. Sat: 8 km easy, then 30 minutes of single-leg RDLs and calf raises. Sun: 30 km, last 5 at goal pace. About 85 km total. Would you change anything?

ok so i wrote a haiku for english class and i kinda want a second opinion before i hand it in
Group chat goes silent—
the typing dots appear, stop,
appear, stop again
thoughts?

I'm opening a cafe that only runs from 8pm until 3am, for night owls, insomniacs and shift workers. The name is "Moth & Ember." Moths come to the light, embers keep glowing after the fire's gone, and that's the mood I want. I'm 31 and a former bartender. Does the name give you the right picture?

I moved here two years ago for university and wrote this on the bus. English isn't my first language, so I'm curious how it lands:
My mother tongue has nine words for rain.
English gave me one and a shrug.
On the bus I whisper them anyway:
the soft one, the sideways one,
the one that means you're late, come in.

I run a small bakery in Tulsa and wrote this for a local business grant application: "We freeze tomorrow's unsold sourdough at closing and sell it as a $12 rescue box to restaurants for croutons and bread pudding, turning our 15% waste into a profit line." Would you give me your feedback?

I'm a new dad (38) and I wrote this lullaby chorus at 3 a.m. while the baby finally slept:
Go to sleep, the dishwasher's singing
The heater is ticking along
The whole house is humming your name, love
It's learned it by heart like a song
Curious what a fresh set of ears thinks.

I'm a carpenter, and I wasted a lot of lumber before I wrote this out. The app is called Kerf. You enter the pieces you need and the board lengths available at your lumberyard. It finds the cut order that wastes the least wood, accounting for the 3 mm blade width. It prints a cut list with each cut numbered on a diagram of the board. Does it sound practical to you?

I'm an amateur astronomer and posted this on Facebook: "Saturn tonight through my $90 telescope: tiny, tilted, impossible, rings like a hat. My daughter asked if it was a sticker on the lens. I said no. She was quiet for a full minute, which has never happened." Tell me what you think!

Wed: during swim lessons, 30 laps. Thu: 20-minute kettlebell video while the kids watch a show. Fri: 15-minute kitchen dance party. Sat: family hike carrying the youngest. Sun: rest. Does this seem sustainable?

I'm launching a green burial company called Return. The symbol is a single leaf, outlined, whose veins branch out in the closed concentric whorls of a fingerprint, so the leaf also reads as a human thumbprint. Deep moss green, slightly uneven line, like it was pressed in ink. Name below in a quiet serif. I'm hoping you can give me an honest response.

I'm a marine biologist and I'm starting a company called Shell Game. We pick up oyster shells from restaurants weekly, a fee of $30 a month, cure them for six months and deliver them to reef restoration projects. Each restaurant receives a plaque: "Your shells built 3 square feet of reef." Photos and GPS coordinates are included each quarter. Would restaurants actually pay? Curious what you think.

Here's the central question of my philosophy dissertation: "If moral testimony is epistemically legitimate in some domains, what explains why deferring to an expert about whether to donate seems acceptable while deferring about whether to forgive does not?" I'd appreciate your feedback.

I lead HR for a call center and I'm applying for a VP role. One bullet I've gone back and forth on: "Redesigned frontline hiring for a 600-employee center, replacing resume screens with 20-minute work-sample calls; 90-day attrition fell from 41% to 19%, saving roughly $730K annually." What's your honest opinion?

Hi! I'm a pastry chef and I've been writing posts for my bakery's site. New one is called "Why Your Croissants Taste Like Bread With Ambitions." It opens: "Butter doesn't melt at 32°C so much as give up, and the exact moment it does is the whole reason your lamination collapses." Thoughts?

I'm a structural engineer. My app idea is CrackCheck. You put a printed 5 cm reference card next to a wall crack and photograph it. Computer vision measures the width to about 0.1 mm. Every month it reminds you to re-shoot from the same angle, using a ghost overlay of the last photo. If the width grows more than 0.3 mm, it tells you to call a professional. Thoughts?

I'm a 20-year-old intern and somehow I was asked to speak for our founder. I said: 'I've known Mr. Reyes for eleven weeks. In that time he learned my name, my coffee order, and the name of my cat. I'm told he also started a company. I'll take people's word for it. But anyone who remembers the intern's cat has already built something that lasts.' Was that too bold?

Retired baker, still experimenting. Rye and caraway sourdough discard crackers: 150g discard, 60g rye flour, 40g olive oil, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp caraway seeds. Mix, rest 30 minutes, roll paper thin, brush with water, and sprinkle with flaky salt and more seeds. Bake at 180°C for 18 minutes, rotating once, until they're deep amber and snap. I'd like a second opinion, please.

I run a little pottery studio and want to stop guessing about cracking. Here's what I wrote in my notebook: "Does adding 5% grog by weight to our stoneware body reduce cracking in pieces thicker than 2 cm during bisque firing at a ramp of 100°C per hour?" I'd fire matched test tiles. Does this seem like a good question to you?

units: I'm 40 and have never lifted before, so I kept it simple. Mon/Wed/Fri: goblet squat, dumbbell bench, one-arm row, Romanian deadlift, plank, always in that order. Start at 3x8, add one rep per week until 3x12, then add weight. Tue/Thu: 20-minute walk. Sat: something fun. Sun: rest. I write down how I felt after each session. I'm a bit nervous about sharing it. What do you think?

I'm a vegan and only a year into cooking. These are king oyster "scallops": cut stems into 2 cm thick rounds, score the tops in a crosshatch, and sear in a dry cast iron pan with a weight on top until deep brown. Then add olive oil and white miso whisked with lemon, and baste for 1 minute. Serve on pea purée with chive oil. How does it sound to you?

I'm a retired schoolteacher with an 8-inch telescope, and I posted this in my astronomy club's group: "Saturn tonight from the back garden. The rings were so sharp I could see the Cassini gap. I woke my wife to look. She said, 'It looks fake.' I said, 'That's the nicest thing anyone's said about it.'" Just a bit of fun, but I'd like your opinion.

Okay, nervous about sharing this, I've only ever shown my cat. Logline for a heist comedy I'm writing: "Three retired piano movers in Glasgow plan the perfect robbery of a concert hall by stealing the Steinway while the pianist is still playing it." What's your opinion?

I'm a grad student who writes songs to cope with deadlines. This chorus is about my grandfather's radio, which I still keep on my desk. Does it work as a chorus, in your view?
He tuned it by feel, a quarter inch of static,
found the ballgame in the hiss like a man finding a door.
Now it sits on my desk, picking up nothing,
but I turn the dial anyway. I just want to hear it once more.
so my brother and I started a small tea company in our garage and this is the slogan I drafted lol: "Sit down. It's steeping." Be honest, what do you think?

I've gardened the same plot for six years. My app idea is a journal that learns your microclimate. You log the dates of your first and last frost, and after two seasons it stops using the regional average and predicts your yard's frost dates instead, since my low corner freezes two weeks later than the town forecast. What do you think of this?

I'm a 62-year-old dairy farmer. At my neighbor Walt's retirement, I said: 'Walt farmed the same hundred and sixty acres as his father. People call that standing still. But I watched him walk that fence line every morning for forty years, and the ground under him changed more than any of us did. You don't stay in one place by not moving. You stay by tending.' Honest feedback welcome.

I'm a vet tech, and kids ask me about death all the time. Premise: Gus's goldfish dies, and at the funeral each relative gives a different eulogy. Gran's is wrong, Dad's is too short, and Gus slowly realizes each of them knew a different fish. Last line: "Gus said his own, and it was the longest." Could you give me your opinion?

I'm a bike mechanic, and I want to open a repair cart outside the train station. You drop your bike at 8 a.m. with a tag that lists the issues, and I text you a quote before 9. If you reply "yes," it's done by 5:30, and you pick it up on your way home. If you reply "no," it's free of charge to wait. No shop rent, just a cart and a trailer. What do you think about this idea?

units: Hello, I'm a baker and just opened a sourdough place in my town. I'm putting this on the paper bags: "Three days to make. Ten minutes to vanish." Could you tell me your opinion?

I own a flower shop and I'm training for my first marathon (week 10 of 16). Mon: rest. Tue: 8 miles easy. Wed: 6 miles with 3x1 mile at tempo. Thu: 5 easy plus strides, 20 min strength. Fri: rest. Sat: 16 mile long run, last 3 at goal pace. Sun: 4 recovery miles. Wedding season hits in May, so Fridays stay empty on purpose. What's your take?

I make furniture as a hobby and wrote this for my profile. I'd be grateful for any feedback.
"I build furniture slowly, and I'd like to date the same way: sand down only what needs it, leave the grain showing. Weekends I'm in a cold garage with the classical station on. If you'd like to hold the other end of a board and talk about nothing in particular, I'd like that."

I write narrative for video games and I'm trying prose for the first time. Here's an opening paragraph:
"The map was wrong in the way maps are wrong when they love you: it left out the cliff, the wolves, the long unfashionable middle of the journey, and drew the sea closer than it was. Imre followed it anyway. You can forgive a lot in something that wanted you to arrive."
How does it come across?

I'm a divorce lawyer, and I write romance on the side under a pen name. Here's my opening line: "The custody agreement gave Dev the house and Priya the sourdough starter, and neither of them, in the end, knew how to keep the thing alive." How does it read to you?

I'm opening a cafe that only runs from 8pm until 3am, for night owls, insomniacs and shift workers. The name is "Moth & Ember." Moths come to the light, embers keep glowing after the fire's gone, and that's the mood I want. I'm 31 and a former bartender. Does the name give you the right picture?

I'm 20, a sophomore working at a campus café. Monthly money is $1,150. Room 520; groceries 180 (Sunday batch cooking); phone 25; textbook fund 50; laundry 20; coffee and friends 80; savings 100; tuition-gap fund 100; clothes 25; unassigned 50. First budget I've ever made. Does it look okay to you? Any advice appreciated!

I'm a hospice night nurse, 43, and my coworkers encouraged me to write this down: "When a hospice nurse notices her dying patients all ask for the same stranger in their final hour, she tracks him down and finds a lonely locksmith who has never met any of them." Tell me what you think, please.

I run a used bookshop and wrote a jazzy little number about it. Here's the chorus. I'd be curious about your reaction, whatever it is.
Every book on this shelf was somebody's Tuesday night,
a train ride, a bathtub, a borrowed flashlight.
I just keep the kettle on and the lamp lit low,
and the dead keep writing to whoever's up.

My partner and I are saving for a house. Combined take-home $9,800: rent 2,400; groceries 700; utilities 220; transit 300; insurance 180; house fund 2,500; index funds 1,800; dining and fun 900; travel 500; giving 300. Rule: if any category overspends, it borrows from fun, never from the house fund. What's your opinion?

units: first paragraph of my letter for the Alder Street community garden, be gentle lol: "Mrs. Okafor planted the first tomato here in 2009, in a lot that held a burned-out Buick. Sixteen summers later, forty families eat from it. The water main beneath it is failing, and replacing it costs $11,200. We're asking you to help keep the tomatoes coming." Thoughts?

I make kombucha to sell at the farmers' market, and I'm designing a project about its pH during fermentation. I'll brew five identical 1 L jars, and test pH with a calibrated meter every 12 hours for 14 days. I'll also record the temperature, and taste-test safely only after day 7. The graph should show when it crosses pH 3.5. What would you say about the design?

I own three laundromats in Cleveland and I'm nervous about sharing this. My pitch: "I'll license the software I wrote that lets customers reserve a specific machine and get a text when their cycle ends, at $40 per location monthly, because it cut my idle machine time by 22%." Honest thoughts?

I dispatch buses and write short emails. This one's for my manager. Opinion?
"Hi Pat, route 14's 7:40 is always 8 minutes late because the school crossing on Elm adds traffic. Drivers have logged it for three weeks. Move the timetable to 7:48 and the complaint calls stop. It costs nothing. Thanks, Ruth."

units:
Hello, I'm a linguist and I wrote this edit distance function for comparing dialect spellings. It only keeps one row in memory:
```python
def levenshtein(a, b):
    prev = range(len(b) + 1)
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            cur.append(min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j-1] + 1, prev[j-1] + (ca != cb)))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]
```
Could you give me your opinion?

I'm a freelance designer and invoice clients in installments. This shows what each client still owes. I aggregated billed and paid separately first so the joins don't multiply rows:
WITH b AS (SELECT client_id, SUM(amount) AS billed FROM invoices GROUP BY 1),
p AS (SELECT i.client_id, SUM(pay.amount) AS paid FROM payments pay JOIN invoices i ON i.id = pay.invoice_id GROUP BY 1)
SELECT c.name, COALESCE(b.billed, 0) - COALESCE(p.paid, 0) AS owed
FROM clients c LEFT JOIN b ON b.client_id = c.id LEFT JOIN p ON p.client_id = c.id
ORDER BY owed DESC;
Thoughts?

Monthly cohort retention for our subscription app. I'm a data scientist and wrote it in one sitting, so tell me if I've missed something.
WITH f AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(date_trunc('month', ordered_at)) AS cohort
  FROM orders GROUP BY 1)
SELECT f.cohort,
  DATEDIFF('month', f.cohort, date_trunc('month', o.ordered_at)) AS months_since,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS active
FROM f JOIN orders o USING (customer_id)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;
